lessons.title: Translation and Explanation of Selected Verses
lessons.notes_html:
Selected Verses - Translations

Verse about fearing for weak offspring: وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا

  • Translation: And those (who fear Allah Almighty) should fear - those who, if they left weak offspring behind them, would fear for their (ruin) - so they should fear Allah and speak straightforward words.

Verse about consuming the wealth of orphans: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا

  • Translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly only consume fire in their bellies, and they will enter a blazing Fire.

Verse about handing over the orphans' wealth: وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا

  • Translation: And hand over to the orphans the wealth that is under your care, and do not exchange their pure and fine wealth for your defective and bad wealth, nor consume their wealth by mixing it with your own wealth, for that is a very great sin.

Verse about women's dower (mahr): وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا

  • Translation: And give women their dower (mahr) happily. Yes, if they willingly give up a part of it for you, then consume it with pleasure and delight.

Verse about trade by mutual consent and not killing yourselves: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا

  • Translation: O believers! Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly among yourselves, except when (the transaction) is trade with your mutual consent (then there is no harm); and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah Almighty is Merciful to you.

Verse about worship of Allah and doing good: وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا

  • Translation: And worship Allah alone, and do not associate anyone with Him; and do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbouring relative, the distant neighbour, the companion by your side, the traveller, and those under your authority. Indeed, Allah does not love the arrogant and boastful (nor those who are miserly).

Verse prescribed for the Children of Israel about killing: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ

  • Translation: For this reason We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a person without (retribution for) a life or (punishment for) corruption in the land, it is as if he killed all mankind; and whoever saves a life, it is as if he saved all mankind. And indeed Our Messengers came to them with clear signs, yet many of them even after that are transgressors in the land.

Verse about the Messenger sent with guidance and the true religion: هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ

  • Translation: He (Allah Almighty) is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the true religion, so that He may make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists dislike it.

Verse about permission to fight: أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ

  • Translation: Permission (to fight) has been given to those against whom the disbelievers wage war, because they have been wronged; and indeed Allah is Able to help them.

Verse about those given power in the land: الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ

  • Translation: Those who, if We give them power in the land, establish Salah, give Zakat, enjoin good and forbid evil; and with Allah is the end of all matters.

Rights of the Orphan - Verse 6 of Surah An-Nisa

  • The orphan should be tested, and when he reaches the age of marriage and maturity (rushd) in managing wealth is seen in him, his wealth should be handed over to him.
  • The orphan's wealth should not be wasted in extravagance (israf), nor consumed hastily out of fear that the orphan will grow up.
  • A guardian who is rich should refrain from (consuming) the orphan's wealth, and one who is poor may consume according to custom.
  • When the orphan's wealth is handed over to him, witnesses should be appointed, and Allah Almighty is sufficient as One who takes account.

Buloogh and Rushd, and Handing Over the Orphan's Wealth

  • Buloogh means reaching the age of marriage. Rushd means possessing sound judgment in managing wealth and business.
  • The method told in the Holy Quran: keep testing the orphans until, when they reach the age of marriage, if you then see any sound judgment in them, hand over their wealth to them; and when you hand over their wealth to them, appoint witnesses over them.
  • Protection of the orphan's wealth is necessary because it is the means of their livelihood and upbringing (Allah Almighty made it the cause of their sustenance); being minor and immature, orphans cannot protect it themselves; even a little negligence can harm both the wealth and its owner; and dishonesty in it is a very great sin.

Responsibilities and Instructions for the Guardian of the Orphan

  • Protect the orphan's wealth and do not commit dishonesty in it.
  • Do not hand over wealth to an immature and minor orphan; instead arrange for his basic needs (food, clothing, education and upbringing).
  • Test the orphan, and when he becomes adult and sound in judgment, hand over his wealth to him in the presence of witnesses.
  • A rich guardian should refrain from the orphan's wealth, and a poor guardian may consume only according to custom.
  • Hand over to the orphan the wealth that is under your care, and do not exchange their pure and fine wealth for your defective and bad wealth, nor consume their wealth by mixing it with your own wealth - that is a very great sin.
  • Do not hand over wealth to an immature and minor orphan; instead, from his wealth, arrange for his needs (food, clothing, education and upbringing) and speak good words to him.

Punishment for Dishonesty in the Orphan's Wealth

  • Those who consume the orphan's wealth unjustly only consume fire in their bellies and will enter a blazing Fire.
  • In Hadith too, consuming the orphan's wealth has been counted among the major sins. (Sahih Bukhari, Kitab-ul-Muharibeen, Hadith: 6857)

Human Life, Wealth and Unlawful Earning

  • The verse about killing states the sanctity of human life and the importance of protecting it. A person becomes a killer when he breaks the bonds of human blood relations, the feeling of sympathy with humanity leaves his heart, and only his own interest remains before him, as a result of which he kills others. Therefore the unjust killing of one innocent human being is as if all humanity has been killed.
  • "Do not kill yourselves" means that in Islam unjust killing is forbidden - neither kill any other human being unjustly, nor kill yourself (suicide). Three things of every human being are of the greatest importance: his life, wealth and honour; Islam guarantees these three things to its followers. Indeed, Allah Almighty is Merciful to you.
  • Unlawful ways of acquiring wealth: consuming wealth by unjust and unlawful means is forbidden. Such things as are themselves forbidden, for example pork, wine and intoxicants - their trade and use is already unlawful and forbidden. And such things as are themselves lawful and permissible, but in whose buying and use some unlawful method is used, also become forbidden, for example theft, robbery, deception, usurping rights, bribery and fraud.

Punishments for Disturbing General Peace and Security

  • For those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land, four kinds of punishments have been fixed: (1) they should be killed, (2) or crucified, (3) or their hands on one side and feet on the other side should be cut off, (4) or they should be exiled from the land.
  • That is disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. But those who repent before you overpower them, then know that Allah Almighty is Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Al-Birr (Goodness), Patience and Silah Rahmi

  • Al-Birr means goodness, and it means doing good and pleasing deeds. In the verse لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ, the following points of Al-Birr have been stated:
  • Beliefs: belief in Allah Almighty, the Day of Judgment, the angels, the Book of Allah Almighty and the Prophets.
  • Dealings: giving wealth, despite love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, travellers, and freeing slaves.
  • Acts of worship: establishing Salah and giving Zakat.
  • Morals: fulfilling a promise when made.
  • Patience: remaining steadfast at times of hardship, suffering and war. These very people are true believers, and they are those who fear Allah Almighty.
  • Three occasions of patience are stated in this verse: (1) the time of hardship, (2) the time of suffering and calamity, (3) the time of war. On these occasions one should remain steadfast.
  • Silah Rahmi means maintaining relations with relatives and loving them and treating them well. Al-Arham is the plural of Rahm, which means blood and close relations; maintaining relations with them is called Silah Rahmi. The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: Silah Rahmi is not that when someone joins with you, you join with him; rather Silah Rahmi is that even if someone breaks with you, you still keep the close relationship joined with him.

The Islamic State and the Duties of Muslim Rulers

  • In the light of verse 41 of Surah Al-Hajj, this verse mentions the virtue of the believers, the prophecy of their rule, the responsibility of the Islamic state, and the qualities of the helpers of the religion. The purpose and qualities of an Islamic state are: if the believers get government, they remain firm in faith, righteous deeds, worship, avoiding shirk, striving for the dominance of the religion, and steadfastness in fear and danger. They establish Salah and also observe Zakat. They use all their authority to spread goodness and remove evil.
  • Establish Salah: Salah is an important pillar of the religion and an act of worship; its purpose is that man's connection with Allah Almighty becomes strong and purity of soul is attained.
  • Pay Zakat: Zakat relates to the economy of society; therefore the state should create economic resources and make proper arrangements for the needs of the people.
  • Enjoin good and forbid evil: use all their authority to spread goodness and remove evil.
  • Provide peace and security to the subjects, and arrange for their education, health and economy. After the migration to Madinah Munawwarah, the first Islamic state came into being, for which the first constitution and charter was made under the name of the Charter of Madinah (Mithaq-e-Madinah), and the Holy Prophet ﷺ was made its head and responsible for making peace among the subjects.

Love for Allah and His Messenger ﷺ

  • In the light of verse 24 of Surah At-Tawbah, believing in Allah Almighty, loving Allah Almighty and the Holy Prophet ﷺ, and striving (jihad) in the way of Allah Almighty come before everything in the world. Faith is the greatest wealth of the world; through it man not only gains benefit in this world but also keeps preparing for the Hereafter.
  • The standard of love of a true believer should be that his fathers, sons, friends, wives, relatives, earned wealth, trade and places of residence - all of these - should not be more beloved to him than Allah and His Holy Messenger, and the love of relatives should not stop him from walking on the path of truth.
  • If a person does not love Allah and His Holy Messenger above all, then he cannot escape the displeasure of Allah Almighty.

Permission to Fight (Izn-e-Qital) and Allah's Help

  • The wisdom of permission to fight (izn-e-qital) stated in the Holy Quran is: to redress the oppressed, to punish the corrupt and the promise-breakers, to bring peace and security in the world, to strive for the exaltation of the word of Allah Almighty, to protect people's lives, wealth, honour and dignity, religion and the sanctity of places of worship from the evil of corrupt people, and to defend the places of worship of the heavenly religions (monasteries, churches, places of worship and mosques).
  • Condition of the Muslims in the Makkan period: the thirteen years in Makkah Mukarramah, from the announcement of Prophethood until the migration to Madinah, were extremely trying years of patience, trial and hardship for the Muslims and for the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself. There, instead of reacting to hardships and difficulties, patience was commanded, and every kind of retaliatory action was forbidden.
  • Amr bil-Ma'roof wa Nahi anil-Munkar: Ma'roof means such good and virtuous deeds which everyone calls good, and Munkar means evil deeds. That is, to enjoin good deeds and to forbid evil deeds.
  • Forms in which help comes from Allah Almighty: (1) Allah is Able to help the oppressed Muslims, and He has promised to help the Muslims. (2) Against the cruel enemies of Islam, Allah Almighty will defend the believers. (3) Those who help the religion of Allah, Allah will surely help them. Indeed, Allah is Powerful, Mighty.

Word Meanings

  • فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ - He should refrain (from it).
  • مَفْرُوضًا - Made obligatory / fixed as compulsory.
  • فَارْزُقُوهُمْ - Feed them / give them.
  • ذُرِّيَّةً - Offspring (ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا: weak offspring).
  • خَافُوا - They fear.
  • بُطُونِ - Bellies.
  • سَعِيرًا - Blazing Fire.
  • لَا تَأْكُلُوا - Do not consume.
  • مُخْتَالًا - Arrogant (one who walks proudly).
  • مُسْرِفُونَ - Those who exceed limits.
  • خِزْيٌ - Disgrace.
  • تَقْدِرُوا - You overpower them / you gain control over them.
  • اِقْتَرَفْتُمْ - You earned.
  • كَرِهَ - They dislike.
  • صَوَامِعُ - Monasteries (hermitages).
  • بِيَعٌ - Churches.
  • مَكَّنَّا - We gave a place / We established.
  • الْيَتَامَى - Orphans.
  • بَثٌّ - Spread / scattered.
  • حُوبًا - Sin.
  • نِحْلَةً - Happily (as a gift).
  • السُّفَهَاءَ - The foolish / those without understanding.

mcqs.q: According to the Holy Quran, what do those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly actually consume in their bellies?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fire. The verse declares that those who consume the orphans' wealth unjustly only consume fire in their bellies, and they will enter a blazing Fire. This shows the extreme seriousness of dishonesty in an orphan's property.

mcqs.q: When an orphan reaches the age of marriage and sound judgment (rushd) is seen in him, what must his guardian do with the orphan's wealth?
options: Hand over the wealth to the orphan
Keep the wealth until the orphan turns forty
Give the whole wealth away in charity
Merge the wealth permanently into his own business
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the guardian must hand over the wealth to the orphan. The Quran instructs that orphans be tested, and when they reach the age of marriage (buloogh) and rushd is seen in them, their wealth is returned to them, and witnesses should be appointed at the handing over.

mcqs.q: In the rules about the orphan's wealth, what does 'rushd' mean?
options: Sound judgment in managing wealth and business
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sound judgment in managing wealth and business. Buloogh means reaching the age of marriage, whereas rushd means the orphan has become sensible enough to handle wealth and business properly, and only then is his wealth handed over to him.

mcqs.q: According to the Holy Quran, how may a poor guardian use the wealth of the orphan under his care?
options: He may take half of it as his fee
He may use it without any limit
He may sell it and keep the profit
He may consume from it according to custom, in a fair and reasonable way
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a poor guardian may consume from the orphan's wealth only according to custom. A guardian who is rich must refrain from the orphan's wealth altogether, while a poor one is allowed only a fair, customary amount, because the wealth belongs to the orphan.

mcqs.q: What does the Holy Quran command about giving women their dower (mahr)?
options: It should be given to them happily
It may be withheld until the end of marriage
It should be returned to the husband's family
It is optional and may be dropped by agreement of the husband alone
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the mahr should be given happily. The verse says: 'And give women their dower (mahr) happily (nihlatan).' Only if the women themselves willingly give up a part of it may the husband consume that part with pleasure and delight.

mcqs.q: Which is the one permitted way of taking one another's wealth mentioned in the verse of Surah An-Nisa?
options: Trade carried on with mutual consent
mcqs.why: The correct answer is trade carried on with mutual consent. Allah Almighty forbids consuming one another's wealth unjustly, except when the transaction is trade with mutual consent; deception, bribery and fraud are all unlawful methods and remain forbidden.

mcqs.q: According to the ruling prescribed for the Children of Israel, killing one person unjustly is counted equal to what?
options: Killing the people of one tribe
mcqs.why: The correct answer is killing all mankind. The Quran states that whoever kills a person without retribution for a life or punishment for corruption in the land, it is as if he killed all mankind, and whoever saves one life, it is as if he saved all mankind.

mcqs.q: According to verse 41 of Surah Al-Hajj, what do believers do when they are given power in the land?
options: They collect taxes and build palaces
They expand their borders and store wealth
They perform Hajj and Umrah every year
They establish Salah, give Zakat, enjoin good and forbid evil
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they establish Salah, give Zakat, enjoin good and forbid evil. These four duties describe the purpose of an Islamic state and the qualities of Muslim rulers in the light of Surah Al-Hajj, verse 41.

mcqs.q: In the verse about Al-Birr, on which three occasions is patience (sabr) mentioned?
options: Hardship, suffering and calamity, and war
mcqs.why: The correct answer is hardship, suffering and calamity, and war. The verse about Al-Birr praises those who remain steadfast at the time of hardship, at the time of suffering, and at the time of war, and calls such people the true believers who fear Allah.

mcqs.q: What is the true meaning of Silah Rahmi according to the saying of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
options: Keeping the bond of kinship joined even with the one who breaks with you
Joining only with those who join with you
Giving gifts only to wealthy relatives
Meeting relatives only on the days of Eid
mcqs.why: The correct answer is keeping the bond joined even with the one who breaks with you. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) explained that Silah Rahmi is not merely returning the favour of the relative who keeps ties with you; it is maintaining the relationship even when the other side cuts it off.
