lessons.title: Introduction to Hadith and Sunnah and Their Effects on Practical Life
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Hadith?

  • Literal meaning: The word "Hadith" means news, talk and a new thing.
  • Technical meaning: The saying (talk), action (deed) and approval (tacit confirmation) of our Master, Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is called Hadith.
  • Hadith is also called "Khabar" and "Sunnah".
  • Rawi (narrator): The people who narrated these hadiths from the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) down to us are called "Rawi"; each one of the people who transmitted the hadith is a Rawi.
  • Sanad-e-Hadith: The chain of narrators is called "Sanad-e-Hadith".
  • Matn: The text of the hadith is called "Matn".

What Is Sunnah?

  • Literal meaning: "Sunnah" means "way" and "path".
  • Technical meaning: The way adopted in the life of the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is called "Sunnah", and it also includes an act which the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) performed repeatedly.
  • Sunnah has been described in the Holy Quran by the name "Uswah Hasanah", which means "the best model".
  • Allah Almighty says (Surah Al-Ahzab: 21): "In the person of the Prophet there is an excellent model for you."

Difference Between Hadith and Sunnah

  • There is only a slight difference between Hadith and Sunnah.
  • Hadith is generally used for sayings.
  • Sunnah is generally used for actions and practice.
  • The word that expresses the meaning of Hadith is Sunnah.

The Four Kinds of Hadith

  • (1) Hadith Qawli: That hadith in which a saying or command of Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is stated, as the Holy Prophet ﷺ said with his blessed tongue. Example: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: أَفْشُوا السَّلَامَ — Translation: Spread salaam. (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 1854)
  • (2) Hadith Fi'li: That hadith in which an act and way of Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is stated, that the Holy Prophet ﷺ did thus. Example: Hazrat Anas (RA) states: The Holy Prophet ﷺ drank goat's milk with yoghurt, then rinsed with water. (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 99)
  • (3) Hadith Taqriri: That hadith in which a Companion performed some act in the presence of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, of which the Holy Prophet ﷺ had knowledge, but he neither stopped him from that act nor praised him for it; rather he remained silent, or the Holy Prophet ﷺ gave permission for that act or expressed his approval. Example: Hazrat Anas (RA) states that he had a little brother "Abu Umair" who had kept a nightingale (bulbul) and used to play with it. The Holy Prophet ﷺ often used to come to our house, but he never forbade keeping that nightingale. (Sahih Bukhari: 6129, Sahih Muslim: 2150)
  • (4) Hadith Qudsi: That hadith whose meaning and purport is from Allah Almighty and whose words are those of our Master, Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, the Seal of the Prophets (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions). Example: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: قَالَ اللهُ: أَنْفِقْ يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ أُنْفِقْ عَلَيْكَ — Translation: Allah said: O son of Adam! Keep spending (on My servants) and I will spend on you. (Sahih Bukhari: 5352)

Effects of Sunnah on Our Practical Life

  • Man strives to fulfil his needs and tasks, but if in those tasks the Sunnah of the Prophet is observed, those tasks are counted as deeds and worship.
  • For example: eating and drinking is our need, but if, with the intention of Sunnah, sitting with dignity at the tablecloth (dastarkhwan) and eating together is arranged, that eating too is worship.
  • Observing the Sunnah of the Prophet provides for the improvement of human health and the environment, because the Sunnah of the Prophet teaches purity and cleanliness in the use of lawful and pleasing things, which closes the door to all diseases.
  • Following the Sunnah of the Prophet ends differences and creates unity and agreement. When all people get a common and general code for living a practical life, the tendency to disunity among them weakens.
  • Following the Sunnah of the Prophet blocks the paths of false and satanic ways. The atmosphere of truth and goodness gets life, which closes the door to all social and moral evils.
  • In many matters, science too has supported the Sunnah, although the Sunnah has no need of the support of science.

Reviving the Sunnah

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever, at the time of corruption of my Ummah, firmly held on to any one of my Sunnahs, for him is the reward of a hundred (100) martyrs.
  • That is, the person who acts upon the Sunnah and revives it in an age of inaction and corruption gets reward equal to a hundred martyrs. (Hilyat-ul-Auliya by Al-Isbahani, Vol. 8, p. 200)

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Hadith'?
options: News, talk and a new thing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is news, talk and a new thing. Literally, 'Hadith' carries these meanings, while in technical terms it refers to the saying, action and approval (tacit confirmation) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

mcqs.q: In technical terms, what is called Hadith?
options: Only the verses of the Holy Quran
The saying, action and approval of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the saying, action and approval of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). Every saying (qawl), deed (fi'l) and tacit approval (taqreer) of the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) is Hadith, which is also called Khabar and Sunnah.

mcqs.q: The chain of narrators through which a hadith reaches us is called what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sanad-e-Hadith. The chain of narrators is the Sanad, the actual text of the hadith is called the Matn, and each person who transmitted the hadith in that chain is called a Rawi (narrator).

mcqs.q: Who is a 'Rawi' in the science of Hadith?
options: The scribe who copied the Quran
A person who narrated and transmitted a hadith
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a person who narrated and transmitted a hadith. The people who narrated the ahadith from the Holy Prophet (PBUH) down to us are called Rawi, and every single transmitter in the chain carries this title.

mcqs.q: By which name has Sunnah been described in the Holy Quran, as in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 21?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Uswah Hasanah, meaning the best model. Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 21 declares: 'In the person of the Prophet there is an excellent model for you,' and Sunnah means the way and path adopted in the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

mcqs.q: A hadith in which a saying or command of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is stated, such as 'Spread salaam', is called what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hadith Qawli. A Qawli hadith reports a saying or command spoken by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) with his blessed tongue; the example 'Spread salaam' is recorded in Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith 1854.

mcqs.q: In which kind of hadith did a Companion perform an act in the presence of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), and he neither stopped him nor praised him, but remained silent or approved?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hadith Taqriri. In a Taqriri hadith the Prophet (PBUH) knew of a Companion's act and kept silent or expressed approval, as in the case of Abu Umair keeping a nightingale, which the Prophet (PBUH) never forbade.

mcqs.q: What is special about a Hadith Qudsi?
options: It was written by the angels
It is a part of the Holy Quran
Its meaning is from Allah Almighty and its words are those of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
It has no chain of narrators
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that its meaning is from Allah and its words are from the Holy Prophet (PBUH). For example: 'Allah said: O son of Adam! Keep spending (on My servants) and I will spend on you' (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith 5352).

mcqs.q: How do ordinary acts like eating and drinking become worship, according to the effects of Sunnah on practical life?
options: When they are done with the intention of following the Sunnah
When they are done in a large gathering
When they are done only on Fridays
mcqs.why: The correct answer is when they are done with the intention of following the Sunnah. Eating and drinking are human needs, but if a person eats sitting with dignity at the dastarkhwan with the intention of Sunnah, that very eating is counted as a deed and worship.

mcqs.q: What reward is promised for the one who firmly holds to a Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH) at the time of corruption of the Ummah?
options: The reward of one hundred martyrs
The reward of freeing ten slaves
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the reward of one hundred martyrs. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that whoever firmly holds on to any one of his Sunnahs at the time of the corruption of his Ummah will receive the reward of a hundred martyrs (Hilyat-ul-Auliya).

lessons.title: Translation and Explanation of Selected Ahadith
lessons.notes_html:
Learning and Teaching the Quran, and Durood

Hadith about learning and teaching the Quran: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 5027)

  • Translation: The best among you is the one who learns the Holy Quran and teaches it to others.

Hadith about sending Durood upon the Holy Prophet ﷺ: أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 484)

  • Translation: On the Day of Judgment, the closest person to me among the people will be the one who sends the most Durood (blessings) upon me.

Love for the Holy Prophet Is the Sign of Faith

Hadith about love for the Holy Prophet ﷺ: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 15)

  • Translation: The faith of none of you is complete until I am more beloved and dear to him than his father, his children and all people.
  • Explanation: In this blessed hadith, love for the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) has been described as the sign of faith. Loving the Holy Prophet ﷺ includes all kinds of love, such as the love of mother, father and dear ones, or those loves which are due to natural or psychological causes.
  • One should keep voluntary love for the Holy Prophet ﷺ, until a person sacrifices even his own desire, his own will, his wealth, children and his life for the commands of Allah Almighty and the Holy Prophet ﷺ; until then he is not a person of perfect faith.

Zikr, Dua and Completion of Faith

  • Zikrullah: In its broad meaning, it includes Salah, recitation of the Quran, dua and istighfar — all of them; but generally, in technical terms, describing the glorification and sanctification of Allah Almighty, His Oneness and purity, His greatness and grandeur, and His perfect attributes is called "Zikrullah".
  • Among all azkar (forms of remembrance), La ilaha illallah has been called the best Zikr, because this Kalima is the collection of all perfect attributes, supreme in greatness and grandeur. It is the most effective in purifying the inner self and turning the heart away from every side and joining it with Allah Almighty; and by reciting it with certainty and truthfulness, man enters Islam and becomes deserving of entering Paradise.
  • Zikr is the cause of peace of heart (satisfaction of heart).
  • Dua: "Dua" is the expression of humility by a weak person when asking from one superior or higher than himself. Dua means supplicating in the court of Allah Almighty while believing Him to be All-Powerful, and presenting a request; dua is a means of attaining one's objective.
  • Four principles of completion of faith (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4681): The Holy Prophet ﷺ stated four principles for the believer which are the means of completion of faith: (1) loving for the sake of Allah, (2) hating for the sake of Allah, (3) giving for the sake of Allah, (4) withholding for the sake of Allah. Whoever acted in this way, indeed his faith has become complete.

Knowledge and Salah

Hadith about seeking knowledge: طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 224)

  • Translation: Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, the importance and virtue of knowledge has been stated, through which the nearness of one's Creator and Master can be attained and every good and evil thing can be recognized, so that we can perform righteous deeds and avoid sins. Therefore we should try to seek knowledge, so that through it we may attain beneficial things, avoid harmful things, and attain success in both worlds.
  • In the hadith, for seeking knowledge, going even to China has been encouraged.

Hadith about Salah: الصَّلَاةُ عِمَادُ الدِّينِ (Ad-Durar Al-Muntashirah fi Al-Ahadith by As-Suyuti, 280)

  • Translation: Salah is the pillar of the religion.
  • Explanation: In this blessed hadith, the virtue and importance of Salah has been stated. Performing Salah five times a day is obligatory upon every sane, adult Muslim man or woman. Through Salah, the servant's connection and contact with Allah Almighty is established. Through Salah alone, the nearness of Allah Almighty, His mercy and pleasure are attained. Therefore we should perform the five daily Salahs with great care and humility, so that our connection and contact with Allah Almighty becomes strong and we may attain His nearness and mercy.

Foundation of Islam, Fasting and Knowledge

  • The foundation of Islam is based on five things: 1. Testimony of Tawheed and Risalah, 2. Establishing Salah, 3. Paying Zakat, 4. Keeping fasts, 5. Performing Hajj of Baitullah (agreed upon).
  • The two statuses of knowledge: (1) Fard-e-Ain — that much knowledge which every person must learn; (2) Fard-e-Kifayah — acquiring the complete knowledge of the religion, and acquiring worldly sciences and arts.
  • In the blessed month of Ramadan, fasting is obligatory upon every sane, adult, resident and healthy person.
  • In the hadith, fasting has been declared a "shield" from the fire of Hell.

Hadith about the virtue of fasting: مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِنْ ذَنْبِهِ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 38)

  • Translation: Whoever kept the fasts of Ramadan with faith and with the intention of reward, (because of it) all his previous sins will be forgiven.

Every Person Is a Guardian

Hadith about guardianship: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُولٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 892)

  • Translation: All of you are guardians, and you will be questioned about your (subjects under your care).
  • Explanation: In this hadith, every person has been declared a guardian. A guardian is every person who has been made responsible for some matters socially or in worldly terms, and the people living under him are called his subjects (ra'iyyat).
  • Among the essential duties of a guardian is also that he is responsible for their training and reform — that is, he teaches each one of them manners and keeps them in good condition.
  • On the Day of Judgment, every person will indeed give account of his deeds, but if someone had a post, position or responsibility in the world, he will also be questioned about his subordinates.

Protecting the Borders of the Homeland

Hadith about guarding the borders (Ribat): رِبَاطُ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صِيَامِ شَهْرٍ وَقِيَامِهِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1913)

  • Translation: Spending one day or one night in jihad is better than fasting for a month and (performing) voluntary worship.
  • Explanation: In this blessed hadith, the virtue and importance of protecting the borders of the Islamic state has been stated: standing guard and protecting and watching over the borders of the country is also counted as jihad.
  • If a guard — that is, an Islamic mujahid — defends the borders for one day or one night, he gets the reward of a whole month's fasts and the night Tahajjud.
  • Therefore we should be full of the spirit of jihad for the exaltation of the word of Allah, and of protecting the homeland and the borders of the homeland, so that no one can look at Islam, the country and the homeland with an evil eye, and the honour of the religion also remains established — and in this lies success in both worlds.

Good Morals, Benefiting People and Giving

Hadith about good morals: أَكْمَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِيمَانًا أَحْسَنُهُمْ خُلُقًا (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4682)

  • Translation: Among you, those with perfect faith are the people whose morals are better than others.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, the virtue and importance of good morals has been stated. "Good morals" has been described as a condition of perfect faith. The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Among you, the most beloved to me is the one who has good morals." (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 6735)

Hadith about benefiting people: خَيْرُ النَّاسِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ (Al-Jami' Al-Kabeer by As-Suyuti, Hadith: 1176)

  • Translation: The good person is the one who benefits people the most.
  • Explanation: In this hadith it has been stated that "being beneficial to people" is necessary for a person to be better. The best person is the one who is beneficial to other people (whether Muslim or non-Muslim).

Hadith about the upper hand: اَلْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 1645)

  • Translation: The upper hand is better than the lower hand.
  • Explanation: In the blessed hadith, by "the upper hand" is meant the giving hand, and by "the lower hand" is meant the taking hand. The upper hand, which provides the needy with the things they need and is generous, is better than the lower hand, and its status is very great.

Harms of Bribery

  • Bribery means every such amount or compensation through which the right of a deserving person is taken away, or something is taken in exchange for some injustice. For example: unlawful gifts, etc.
  • Taking and giving bribes is among the major sins.
  • When the practice of bribery becomes common in a nation, justice, fairness and civility end there, and the unlawful demands of cruel officials become obstacles in the way of people getting their lawful rights; or in acquiring earnings, the right of a deserving person is taken away, and it becomes difficult for people to get their rights and concessions by lawful means.
  • For this reason, the Holy Prophet ﷺ cursed those who take and give bribes. (Sunan Nasa'i: 2631)

Hajj and Sincerity (Ikhlas)

Hadith about Hajj: مَنْ حَجَّ لِلَّهِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ (Sahih Al-Bukhari: 1521)

  • Translation: Whoever performed Hajj for Allah Almighty, and then neither spoke obscenely nor abused, nor committed any sin, he returned from Hajj like the day he was born from his mother's womb.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, the virtue and importance of Hajj has been stated. Hajj is the last and completing pillar among the pillars of Islam, which is obligatory once upon every sane, adult, healthy and capable person. Whoever shows patience during Hajj and stays away from every kind of vain and obscene talk, foul language, every kind of disobedience and sins, he becomes as clean and pure from sins as he was sinless on the day of birth.

Hadith about sincerity (Ikhlas): إِنَّ اللهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَجْسَامِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 2564)

  • Translation: Indeed, Allah Almighty does not look at your bodies and faces, but looks at your hearts.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, the importance of sincerity (ikhlas) has been stated. A person's outward and inward should be one. Whatever good deed is done, it should be done only to attain the pleasure of Allah Almighty; in it there should be no worldly motive, show-off, desire for fame, or motive of any compensation. If the deed is one of sincerity and piety, it is accepted and approved by Allah Almighty, and its reward is also given.

Six Rights of a Muslim over a Muslim

Hadith about the rights of a Muslim: لِلْمُسْلِمِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ سِتٌّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 2637)

  • In this hadith, the exhortation to fulfil the six special rights that a Muslim has over another Muslim under the Islamic relationship in daily practical life has been stated: (1) When he meets a Muslim, he should greet him with salaam (Assalamu Alaikum), (2) and when he invites him, he should accept it, (3) when he sneezes, he should say Yarhamukallah (May Allah have mercy on you), (4) and when he is sick, he should visit him, (5) and when he dies, he should join his funeral, (6) and whatever he likes for himself, he should like for the other too.
  • This creates a shared bond between two Muslims, and strengthens it. The saying of Allah Almighty is: "Believers are brothers among themselves." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 10)
  • When someone meets someone, he says: Assalamu Alaikum.

Branches of Faith and Haya

  • Among the branches of faith, the highest branch is saying La ilaha illallah, because through it alone, the affirmation of Tawheed takes place.
  • The last (lowest) branch is removing a harmful thing from the path. (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 35)
  • Haya (modesty) is such a quality and characteristic of a person which stops a person from immorality, and from many evils and sins. Haya is an important branch of faith.

Guiding to Good, Avoiding Suspicion, Helping the Needy

Hadith about guiding to goodness: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1893)

  • Translation: Whoever guided a person towards goodness, he too will get the same reward as the one who does the good deed.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, the exhortation and support for doing goodness and kindness, and cooperating with one another for goodness and kindness, has been given. Through good advice, guidance, and education and training, the helper too will get as much reward as the doer of that deed gets. Therefore we should ourselves also do goodness and kindness, and also encourage others towards goodness.

Hadith about suspicion (Zann): إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 6066)

  • Translation: Beware of suspicion; suspicion is the biggest lie.
  • Explanation: In this hadith, suspicion has been forbidden. Saying something about someone by guesswork, without investigation and certain knowledge of a thing, is called "Zann" or suspicion.
  • If goodness is intended in it, that is "Husn-e-Zann" (good opinion), which is a pleasing quality, and it has been encouraged. Especially, keeping "Husn-e-Zann" with Allah Almighty is worship. The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Husn-e-Zann" is good worship. (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 7956)
  • If an evil opinion is held about someone, it is termed "bad suspicion" (badgumani) — that is, doubting someone's intention and not keeping a good thought about him in one's heart without reason is called bad suspicion. It has been forbidden in the Holy Quran: "O believers! Avoid suspicions, for that is a sinful act." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 12)
  • Until the investigation about a person is done, you should not hold suspicion about him, because gradually this suspicion turns into hatred and enmity of hearts, which is a sin.

Hadith about helping the needy and the afflicted: مَنْ نَفَّسَ عَنْ مُؤْمِنٍ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ الدُّنْيَا نَفَّسَ اللهُ عَنْهُ كُرْبَةً مِنْ كُرَبِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، مَنْ يَسَّرَ عَلَى مُعْسِرٍ يَسَّرَ اللهُ عَلَيْهِ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 2699)

  • Translation: Whoever removed any of the worldly hardships of a believer, Allah Almighty will save him from hardships on the Day of Judgment; and whoever gave any facility to a person in difficulty, Allah Almighty will create ease for him in this world and the Hereafter.
  • Explanation: Here two matters of Huqooq-ul-Ibad have been made clear: (1) If a believer is in some hardship, calamity or distress, then helping to remove his hardship in such a situation is also a great act of worship, for which the Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is engaged in the work of his brother, Allah Almighty makes his works easy." (Muslim: 2699)
  • (2) If a believer is needy, sick, poor and destitute, serving him and helping him financially, and if a debtor has taken a loan from someone, giving him respite in the loan and providing him facility, is also a deed of very great reward. Allah Almighty will create ease for him in this world and the Hereafter.

Neighbours, Guests and Relatives

  • Three kinds of neighbours (Surah An-Nisa: 36): In the Holy Quran, the command of "good conduct with neighbours" has been given, and three kinds of it have been stated: 1. A neighbour who is a relative, 2. One who is only a neighbour, 3. And one who stayed with you temporarily for some time — for example: a classmate, a companion of a meeting, a journey, or some gathering, etc. Therefore, good conduct should be shown to all neighbours.
  • Ikram-uz-Zaif (honouring the guest): When a person travels and reaches someone for some purpose, he is called a "guest". Asking him the purpose of his coming in a proper manner, behaving with him respectfully, arranging for his lodging, food and drink, and rest, and honouring him according to his status is "honouring the guest".
  • Silah Rahmi: Sharing in the joys and sorrows of one's close dear ones and relatives, helping them in times of need, treating them well, and sympathising with them is called "Silah Rahmi".
  • In the hadith, the benefit of Silah Rahmi has been stated to be abundance of sustenance.

Word Meanings and Key Terms

  • Husn-e-Akhlaq (good morals): In living life, in observing the principles and rules of the religion, treating others well instead of causing them pain, behaving gently, and carrying out one's responsibilities happily while helping them financially, is called "Husn-e-Akhlaq".
  • Signs of a good person: The sign of being the best person is that he is beneficial to other people (whether Muslim or non-Muslim) — one who benefits others, does not cause them pain, and arranges for their food, drink and other facilities.
  • Bribery: Every such amount or compensation through which the right of a deserving person is taken away, or something is taken in exchange for some injustice — for example, unlawful gifts, etc. In the hadith, the one who takes bribes has been declared deserving of curse.
  • Ikhlas (sincerity): Whatever good deed is done, it should be done only to attain the pleasure of Allah Almighty; in it there should be no worldly motive, show-off, desire for fame, or motive of any compensation. A person's outward and inward should be one. A deed done for the pleasure of Allah is called Ikhlas.
  • Zann: Saying something about someone by guesswork, without investigation and certain knowledge of a thing, is called "Zann" or suspicion.
  • Husn-e-Zann: If goodness is intended in Zann, it is "Husn-e-Zann" (good opinion), which is a pleasing quality; "more beloved among people" means Ahabb-un-Nas.
  • Fard-e-Ain: Every person, whether man or woman, must learn that much knowledge through which he understands the necessary matters of belief, lawful and unlawful, pure and impure, permissible and impermissible, and his responsibilities.
  • Fard-e-Kifayah: Acquiring the complete knowledge of the religion, and acquiring worldly sciences and arts, is Fard-e-Kifayah.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sahih Al-Bukhari (5027), who is the best among the people?
options: The one who learns the Holy Quran and teaches it to others
The one who memorises the most poetry
The one who owns the most wealth
The one who travels the most
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who learns the Holy Quran and teaches it to others. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'The best among you is the one who learns the Holy Quran and teaches it,' showing the high rank of both learning and teaching the Quran.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Tirmidhi (484), who will be the closest person to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on the Day of Judgment?
options: The one who built the largest mosque
The one who gave the most charity in secret only
The one who sends the most Durood (blessings) upon him
The one who fasted the most voluntary fasts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who sends the most Durood upon him. The hadith states that on the Day of Judgment, the closest person to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) among the people will be the one who sends the most blessings (Durood) upon him.

mcqs.q: Which Zikr has been called the best of all forms of remembrance (azkar)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is La ilaha illallah. Among all azkar, this Kalima has been called the best Zikr because it gathers all the perfect attributes of Allah, purifies the inner self, and by reciting it with certainty and truthfulness a person enters Islam.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Abi Dawood (4681), which set of four principles completes a believer's faith?
options: Eating less, sleeping less, speaking less and travelling less
Loving for Allah's sake, hating for Allah's sake, giving for Allah's sake and withholding for Allah's sake
Reading, writing, trading and farming for Allah's sake
Fasting, Hajj, Umrah and sacrifice for Allah's sake
mcqs.why: The correct answer is loving, hating, giving and withholding, all for the sake of Allah. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) stated these four principles, and said that whoever acts in this way, his faith has indeed become complete.

mcqs.q: In the hadith, Salah (prayer) has been described as what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the pillar of the religion. The hadith 'As-Salatu Imad-ud-Din' teaches that Salah is the pillar of Islam; performing the five daily prayers is obligatory upon every sane, adult Muslim, and through Salah the servant's connection with Allah is established.

mcqs.q: In the hadith, fasting has been declared as what against the fire of Hell?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a shield. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared fasting to be a shield from the fire of Hell, and fasting in Ramadan is obligatory upon every sane, adult, resident and healthy Muslim.

mcqs.q: What does the hadith 'All of you are guardians' (Sahih Al-Bukhari, 892) teach?
options: Every person should guard his own house only
Every person is responsible for those under his care and will be questioned about them
Only rulers are responsible for people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that every person is responsible for those under his care. The hadith declares every person a guardian (ra'i) over his subjects (ra'iyyat), and on the Day of Judgment he will also be questioned about the people who were under his responsibility.

mcqs.q: According to Sahih Muslim (1913), guarding the borders of the country (Ribat) for one day and night is better than what?
options: Giving all one's wealth in charity
Fasting for a month and voluntary worship of a month
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fasting for a month and a month's voluntary worship. The hadith about Ribat states that spending one day or one night guarding the borders is better than fasting for a month and standing in voluntary worship for a month, because protecting the homeland is also Jihad.

mcqs.q: In the hadith of the 'upper hand' and the 'lower hand', what does the upper hand mean?
options: The giving hand, which provides for the needy
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the giving hand. By 'the upper hand' is meant the hand that gives and is generous to the needy, and by 'the lower hand' the hand that takes; the upper hand is better and its status is very great (Sunan Abi Dawood, 1645).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is one of the six rights of a Muslim over another Muslim, as listed in Sunan Tirmidhi (2637)?
options: Lending him money whenever he asks
mcqs.why: The correct answer is saying 'Yarhamukallah' when he sneezes. The six rights are: greeting with salaam on meeting, accepting his invitation, saying Yarhamukallah when he sneezes, visiting him when sick, joining his funeral when he dies, and liking for him what one likes for oneself.

lessons.title: Belief in Tauheed (Oneness of Allah)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Tawheed

  • Tawheed — literal meaning: The literal meaning of the word "Tawheed" is "to consider One and to believe as One".
  • In the terminology of religion, the belief of Tawheed means that the Creator, Master and Controller of everything in this universe is Allah Almighty alone.
  • He is only One; He has no partner.
  • Believing this belief with firm conviction of the heart, and expressing and confessing it with the tongue when needed and at the right time, is called the belief of Tawheed.

Allah Almighty — Creator and True God

  • Allah Almighty has always existed and will always remain; He alone is the true object of worship.
  • He created every thing of this universe in balance and its system with complete calculation.
  • He has knowledge of every particle of the universe; His sight is over the whole universe.
  • He hears all, provides sustenance to all, and guides them.
  • There is none like Him or equal to Him; He alone is the Master of the benefit and harm of creation.
  • There is none besides Him; He alone will give everlasting life again after death.

Requirements of Tawheed

  • The basic requirements of Tawheed, upon which it is necessary to believe and act, are:
  • (1) Without example: The Being of Allah Almighty is without example. Nothing in the universe is like Allah Almighty — "There is nothing like Him" (Surah Ash-Shura, verse: 11). So Allah Almighty should be believed as an unparalleled Being.
  • (2) His pleasure alone: Only Allah Almighty is the One for whose pleasure man should strive.
  • (3) Worship for Him alone: All deeds that come under worship should be reserved for Allah Almighty alone.
  • (4) Feelings for Him alone: All emotions and feelings should be reserved for Allah Almighty alone, in which the spirit of worship is found: Hamd, Shukr, hope, Tawakkul, fear, Taqwa, true love, devotion, humility and submission, etc.
  • (5) Supreme Ruler and Lawgiver: The true Supreme Ruler of this whole universe should be believed to be Allah Almighty alone. The true Lawgiver is also He alone. Making laws for the life of creation, forgiving them or punishing them is His right alone.
  • (6) Life by His guidance: Life should be spent in this world according to the guidance and command sent by Allah Almighty.
  • (7) Faith with His attributes: Faith should be brought in Allah Almighty along with all His attributes.

Meaning of Iman

  • By Aqeedah are meant those thoughts and ideas in which man holds firm belief, which affect man's character and behaviour.
  • The meaning of Iman is also this same firm belief.

What is Ibadat (Worship)?

  • Reserving all those deeds for Allah Almighty which come under worship is called Ibadat.
  • For example: worshipping none besides Him, vows and offerings also being for Him, asking duas from Him, seeking refuge from Him, and calling upon Him alone for unseen help.

Effects of the Belief in Tawheed

  • Believing in the names and attributes of the Being of Allah Almighty creates love and reverence for Allah Almighty in the servant's heart, as a result of which he becomes obedient to the commands of Allah Almighty.
  • Tawheed grants man the highest station of freedom and liberty.
  • It creates qualities like piety, self-respect and self-honour in man.
  • It creates humility and humbleness in man.
  • Man looks at the whole creation with love and affection with a broad outlook, because it is the creation of Allah Almighty.
  • It creates in man the power of steadfastness, courage, contentment, needfulness, determination, courage, patience and Tawakkul.
  • Because of complete trust in the mercy of Allah Almighty, he never becomes disappointed and hopeless.
  • It creates in man the concept of the unity and equality of mankind.

Allah is Eternal (Azali) and Everlasting (Abadi)

Surah Al-Hadid, verse 3: هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ

  • Translation: He is the First and the Last.
  • Its meaning is: when there was nothing, He still existed; and in the end too, there will be nothing, but He will exist.
  • He has always existed and will always remain. No one created Him.

First Duty and Basis of Salvation

  • A Muslim should first of all correct his belief.
  • The basis of man's welfare and salvation is faith and good deeds.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of the word 'Tawheed'?
options: To consider One and to believe as One
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to consider One and to believe as One. In the terminology of religion, Tawheed means believing with firm conviction of the heart that the Creator, Master and Controller of everything in the universe is Allah Almighty alone, and He has no partner.

mcqs.q: Which verse of Surah Ash-Shura (verse 11) expresses that Allah Almighty is without example?
options: 'He is the First and the Last'
'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'There is nothing like Him' (Surah Ash-Shura, verse 11). This is the first requirement of Tawheed: the Being of Allah is without example, nothing in the universe is like Him, so He must be believed as an unparalleled Being.

mcqs.q: According to the requirements of Tawheed, who alone is the Supreme Ruler and Lawgiver of the universe?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allah Almighty alone. Among the requirements of Tawheed is believing that the true Supreme Ruler of the whole universe and the true Lawgiver is Allah alone; making laws for creation, forgiving them or punishing them is His right alone.

mcqs.q: What does Ibadat (worship) mean in relation to Tawheed?
options: Reserving all deeds that come under worship for Allah Almighty alone
Performing only the five daily prayers
Giving charity to the poor only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is reserving all deeds of worship for Allah alone. Vows and offerings, asking duas, seeking refuge and calling upon Him alone for unseen help are all Ibadat, and none besides Allah may be worshipped in any of these ways.

mcqs.q: What is meant by the words of Surah Al-Hadid, verse 3: 'He is the First and the Last'?
options: Allah created the first man and the last prophet
Allah knows the beginning and end of every nation
Allah has always existed and will always remain; no one created Him
Allah is the first to forgive and the last to punish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah has always existed and will always remain. When there was nothing, He still existed, and in the end too there will be nothing but He will exist; He is Azali (Eternal) and Abadi (Everlasting), and no one created Him.

mcqs.q: Which freedom does the belief in Tawheed grant to man?
options: The highest station of freedom and liberty
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the highest station of freedom and liberty. Tawheed frees man from the slavery of every other power, and along with this it creates piety, self-respect, humility, steadfastness, courage, contentment, patience and Tawakkul in him.

mcqs.q: What concept about mankind is created by the belief in Tawheed?
options: The unity and equality of mankind
The superiority of one nation over others
The separation of people by wealth
The ranking of people by language
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the unity and equality of mankind. Because the whole of creation belongs to one Creator, a believer looks at all creation with love and a broad outlook, and Tawheed removes every basis of discrimination among human beings.

mcqs.q: Which feelings and emotions should be reserved for Allah Almighty alone, according to the requirements of Tawheed?
options: Hamd, gratitude, hope, Tawakkul, fear, Taqwa and true love
Attachment to one's own tribe only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hamd, gratitude, hope, Tawakkul, fear, Taqwa and true love. All emotions in which the spirit of worship is found must be reserved for Allah alone, just as worship itself and the striving for His pleasure belong to Him alone.

mcqs.q: What is the basis of man's welfare and salvation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is faith and good deeds. A Muslim should first of all correct his belief, because the foundation of his welfare and salvation in this world and the Hereafter is Iman together with righteous deeds.

mcqs.q: What is meant by 'Aqeedah'?
options: The list of a person's relatives
Those thoughts and ideas in which man holds firm belief, which affect his character and behaviour
The daily routine of a person
mcqs.why: The correct answer is firm beliefs that affect character and behaviour. Aqeedah means those thoughts and ideas held with firm conviction, and Iman has this same meaning of firm belief, which is why beliefs shape a person's conduct.

lessons.title: Belief in Risalat (Prophethood)
lessons.notes_html:
Literal Meaning of Nubuwwat and Risalah

  • "Nubuwwat" is derived from the word "Naba", which means news. The one who gives news is called "Nabi", whose plural is Anbiya.
  • "Risalah" means conveying the message, and the one who conveys the message is called "Rasool", whose plural is "Rusul".
  • So, the one who gives news is called a "Nabi", and the one who conveys the message is called a "Rasool"; the person who holds the office of Nubuwwat and Risalah is called a Nabi or Rasool.

Technical Meaning of Nubuwwat and Risalah

  • In the terminology of religion, "Nubuwwat and Risalah" is a high spiritual office, for which Allah Almighty chooses special servants from among His servants.
  • Through it, human beings attain the knowledge of Allah (Ma'rifat-e-Ilahi).
  • It is such an office which works to establish a connection between Allah Almighty and His servants.
  • Through it, Allah Almighty conveys His commands and guidance to His servants; through it, He guides, reforms and trains human beings.
  • Even before receiving Risalah, the status of a Rasool in his nation is high and exalted. He is innocent, pure, soft-spoken, of good nature, truthful and trustworthy.
  • Nubuwwat and Risalah is an office which Allah Almighty grants to His specially chosen servants.

The Belief in Risalah

  • The belief in Risalah is the second important and basic belief of Islam.
  • Believing in the Nabi and Rasool is obligatory.

Surah Al-Baqarah: 285: كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ

  • Translation: All believe in Allah, His angels, His books and His Prophets, and say: we make no distinction between any of His Prophets.
  • Allah Almighty sent a Prophet for the guidance and leadership of every nation, and the first Prophet sent by Allah Almighty is Hazrat Adam (AS).

Why Nubuwwat and Risalah are Needed

  • The purpose of man's creation and life has been stated as "the servitude and obedience of Allah Almighty", and that is the thing on which man's success and salvation in this world and the Hereafter depends.
  • Man naturally wants that for practical life there should be before him some example or model, seeing which he may live his life accordingly; in this respect the lives of the Prophets are the best example or an excellent model of conduct for human beings.
  • Allah Almighty sends down a book upon the Prophets for the guidance of His servants.
  • According to Islamic belief, this world is the place of action, and the Hereafter is the place of accountability and questioning.
  • Just as Allah Almighty has arranged to fulfil man's physical needs, in the same way He arranged Nubuwwat and Risalah to fulfil spiritual needs.

Obedience (Ita'at) and Following (Ittiba)

  • Ita'at (obedience) is derived from the word "Taw'", which means the inclination of the heart and obeying or accepting a command. In obedience, one has to submit oneself completely to someone; it cannot be that some commands are obeyed and some are not. The attitude of accepting firm obedience with the attachment of the heart is called "Ita'at".
  • Ittiba (following) is following every step and every manner of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) with true love of the heart, complete inclination of nature, and deep attachment — that is, when heartfelt love is joined with complete obedience, it is called Ittiba.
  • Obedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is that in all matters of life, whatever commands he gave, or guidance he gave, or whatever act he performed, it should be obeyed and acted upon.
  • The real reason for commanding obedience to the Messenger is that Allah Almighty wants His own obedience, and the only means of Allah Almighty's obedience is the Messenger, because Allah Almighty does not speak directly to His servants; rather He speaks only through His Messenger, and the Messenger informs the servants of the guidance of Allah Almighty and His commands.
  • In this respect, obedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is in fact obedience to Allah Almighty: "Whoever obeyed the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), indeed he obeyed Allah." (Surah An-Nisa, verse: 80).

Our Four Relationships with the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • Our four basic relationships with the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) are: (1) Iman, (2) obedience, (3) following, and (4) love.
  • The chain of Nubuwwat was completed with the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), and the belief in the Finality of Prophethood (Khatm-e-Nubuwwat) is an essential part of faith.

Love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ

  • Hubb or love is the name of a natural attraction and a natural feeling; if this love is on the basis of a religious relationship, it is called "spiritual love" or "faith-based love".
  • The blessed person of the Holy Prophet ﷺ deserves every kind of love from us, and it is also a requirement of faith, because this person is the Beloved of Allah Almighty and the benefactor and guide of the believers.
  • Allah Almighty commands us to love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Rather, in the sight of Allah Almighty, that faith and obedience is not even credible whose foundation is not upon the love of the Messenger of Allah.
  • The standard of this love has been stated to be that the Holy Prophet ﷺ deserves more love from them than even their own lives (Al-Ahzab: 6).
  • Love for the Messenger has been declared the sign of faith, and the sign of perfect faith is love for the Messenger (Hubb-e-Rasool): "None of you can be a believer until he loves me more than his parents, children and all people." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Kitab-ul-Iman, Hadith: 15).

Belief in Khatm-e-Nubuwwat (Finality of Prophethood)

  • The literal meaning of "Khatm" is to seal and to complete a task and be free from it.
  • The meaning of Khatm-e-Nubuwwat is that the chain of Nubuwwat, which began with Hazrat Adam (AS), and after which many Prophets came one after another, ended with the Holy Prophet ﷺ. Now, after the Holy Prophet ﷺ, no Prophet will come.
  • With Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the chain of Nubuwwat was completed, and the religion became complete.

Al-Ma'idah: 3: الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا

  • Translation: Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favours upon you, and chosen Islam as the religion for you.

Surah Al-Ahzab: 40: مَا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِنْ رِجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ

  • Translation: Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions) is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: In my Ummah, (30) thirty such liars will come, each of whom will claim to be a Prophet, whereas I am the last Prophet; there is no Prophet after me. (Abu Dawood, Hadith 4253).
  • Need for Khatm-e-Nubuwwat: When the religion became complete, and the clear expression of the pleasure of Allah Almighty upon the religion of Islam took place, and the announcement of the Holy Prophet ﷺ being the last Prophet and Messenger was made, then there remained no need for any new Prophet.
  • Therefore, whoever claims Prophethood in any way after the Holy Prophet ﷺ is a disbeliever and out of the fold of Islam.

Characteristics of the Last Risalah

  • The characteristics of the last Risalah of the Holy Prophet ﷺ are:
  • Universality and worldwide scope.
  • Renewal of the earlier Shariahs.
  • Completeness.
  • Protection of the Book.
  • Protection of the Sunnah of the Prophet.
  • Comprehensiveness, and the Finality of Prophethood (Khatm-e-Nubuwwat).

mcqs.q: The word 'Nubuwwat' is derived from 'Naba'. What does 'Naba' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is news. 'Nubuwwat' comes from 'Naba' meaning news, so the one who gives news is called a Nabi, whose plural is Anbiya; 'Risalah' means conveying the message, and the one who conveys it is called a Rasool, whose plural is Rusul.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Prophet sent by Allah Almighty?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Adam (AS). Allah Almighty sent a Prophet for the guidance and leadership of every nation, and the very first Prophet He sent was Hazrat Adam (AS), with whom the chain of Nubuwwat began.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nisa, verse 80, what is the result of obeying the Messenger of Allah (PBUH)?
options: He becomes free from all duties
He no longer needs the Quran
Whoever obeyed the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that obeying the Messenger is obeying Allah. Allah does not speak directly to His servants; He speaks through His Messenger, so obedience to the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) is in fact obedience to Allah Almighty (Surah An-Nisa, verse 80).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Ita'at (obedience) and Ittiba (following)?
options: Ita'at is for Allah and Ittiba is for parents
Ittiba means obeying only some commands
Ittiba is obedience joined with heartfelt love, following every step and manner of the Messenger
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Ittiba is obedience joined with heartfelt love. Ita'at means submitting completely to the commands, while Ittiba means following every step and manner of the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) with true love of the heart and deep attachment.

mcqs.q: Which four are our basic relationships with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Iman, obedience, following and love. These are the four basic relationships of a believer with the Holy Prophet (PBUH), and along with them the belief in Khatm-e-Nubuwwat is an essential part of faith.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Khatm' in Khatm-e-Nubuwwat?
options: To seal and to complete a task and be free from it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to seal and to complete a task. Khatm-e-Nubuwwat means that the chain of Nubuwwat, which began with Hazrat Adam (AS), was sealed and completed with the Holy Prophet (PBUH), and now no Prophet will come after him.

mcqs.q: By which title is the Holy Prophet (PBUH) described in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 40?
options: Khatam-un-Nabiyyin, the Seal of the Prophets
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Khatam-un-Nabiyyin, the Seal of the Prophets. Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 40 declares that Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, confirming the Finality of Prophethood.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sunan Abi Dawood (4253), how many liars will appear in the Ummah claiming to be prophets?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is thirty. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that in his Ummah thirty such liars will come, each of whom will claim to be a Prophet, whereas he is the last Prophet and there is no Prophet after him.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of the last Risalah of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
options: It was meant only for the people of Arabia
It requires a new prophet after some centuries
Its Book has not been protected
mcqs.why: The correct answer is its universality and worldwide scope. The characteristics of the last Risalah include universality, renewal of the earlier Shariahs, completeness, protection of the Book, protection of the Sunnah, comprehensiveness and Khatm-e-Nubuwwat.

mcqs.q: What is the status of a person who claims prophethood after the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
options: He is a disbeliever and out of the fold of Islam
He is a mistaken but believing Muslim
He is a scholar with a different opinion
He is a reformer of the religion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he is a disbeliever and out of the fold of Islam. Because the religion became complete and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was announced as the last Prophet, no need for a new Prophet remained, and whoever claims prophethood is outside Islam.

chapters.title: Ibadat — Importance of Worship and Jihad

lessons.title: Importance and Benefits of Worship
lessons.notes_html:
What Ibadat Means

  • Ibadat is an Arabic word derived from "Abd".
  • Its literal meaning is: servitude, humility, humbleness, obedience and submission.
  • Its Shariah (technical) meaning is: living one's life according to the Uswah Hasanah of the Holy Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family and companions), with the intention of attaining the pleasure of Allah Almighty, is called "Ibadat".
  • Ibadat includes every act which Allah Almighty has commanded to do, or forbidden to do, because it is the servant's job to obey his Master.
  • Especially if that Master is the King of kings, then considering His commands as a cause of happiness, joy and contentment for oneself is the highest achievement of a servant.

Importance of Ibadat

  • In Islam, after the correctness of faith or belief, emphasis has been laid on Ibadat.
  • These acts of worship are the practical form of direct contact, connection and nearness with Allah Almighty.
  • Allah Almighty says: "And I created the jinn and mankind only that they may worship Me" (Az-Zariyat: 56) — so Allah Almighty created human beings and jinn for worship, and the purpose of creating man is to worship Allah.
  • Allah Almighty says: "O mankind! Worship your Lord who created you and those before you, so that you may be saved (from His punishment)" (Surah Al-Baqarah: 21).

Purpose of Ibadat — Taqwa

  • In Surah Al-Baqarah: 21, the purpose of Ibadat has been stated as "Taqwa".
  • Taqwa is the stage after the purity of the heart, the cleanliness of the soul, and the sincerity of action.
  • It is that heartfelt condition of man, by which the desire to do good deeds and hatred for evils is created.

Surah Al-An'am: 162: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ

  • Translation: Say: my Salah and my sacrifice, and my living and my dying are all for Allah, the Lord of the worlds.
  • In this verse, a brief and comprehensive outline of the straight path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem) has been presented, which is the soul of Islamic life and the life of Islamic society.
  • Every breath, every step and every deed of a Muslim is for Allah Almighty — not for anyone besides Allah or for the desires of one's own self; this is the purpose and intent of a Muslim's life.

Requirements of Ibadat

  • We should accept all the commands of Allah Almighty, act upon them, leave whatever He has declared forbidden, and fulfil whatever He has declared obligatory and compulsory, thus obeying Allah Almighty completely.
  • Every sphere of life should be brought within the circle of the obedience of Allah Almighty — that is, complete obedience should be observed.
  • The saying of Allah Almighty is: "O believers! Enter Islam completely" (Al-Baqarah: 208).

Effects of Ibadat on General Life

  • It creates feelings of love and sympathy for mankind in man; therefore a Muslim keeps love and affection for other people, sympathises with them, and helps them in their joys and sorrows.
  • These acts of worship also teach the lesson of patience and tolerance, and at the same time create the spirit of sacrificing one's personal interest for the pleasure of Allah Almighty and the collective benefit.
  • Acts of worship teach us the lesson of living together with society; therefore man learns to live together with other people, and society becomes likeable.
  • Observing Ibadat ends bad habits like laziness, idleness and wasting time.
  • By observing Salah, qualities of punctuality, outward and inward purity and cleanliness, obedience to the leader, and collectivity are created in man, and he is saved from immodesty and shamelessness.
  • Fasting creates Taqwa in man — that is, the fear of God makes man distinguish between good and evil.
  • Through Zakat, the love of wealth decreases in man, and he feels happiness in helping financially people like himself.
  • Hajj teaches the lesson of collectivity on a worldwide level.
  • By acts like helping people, Silah Rahmi, and supporting the people under one's care, mutual interaction and relations improve.
  • These effects of Ibadat are attained by the believer on the basis of his intention and sincerity; correctness of intention and sincerity in Ibadat are the key to its acceptance.
  • These acts of worship, along with the reform of man, become the means of spreading goodness and virtues in society, and become the cause of worldly and Hereafter prosperity for the believer.

mcqs.q: From which word is 'Ibadat' derived, and what is its literal meaning?
options: From 'Abd'; it means servitude, humility, obedience and submission
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Ibadat is derived from 'Abd' and means servitude, humility, obedience and submission. In Shariah terms, Ibadat means living one's life according to the Uswah Hasanah of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) with the intention of attaining the pleasure of Allah.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Az-Zariyat, verse 56, for what purpose did Allah create the jinn and mankind?
options: Only to rule over other creatures
Only that they may worship Him
mcqs.why: The correct answer is only that they may worship Him. Allah Almighty says: 'And I created the jinn and mankind only that they may worship Me,' so worship is the very purpose of man's creation, and after correctness of faith, Islam lays the greatest emphasis on Ibadat.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 21, what is the purpose of Ibadat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Taqwa. In Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 21, mankind is commanded to worship their Lord who created them and those before them, 'so that you may be saved,' and the purpose of Ibadat is stated as Taqwa.

mcqs.q: What is described in Surah Al-An'am, verse 162: 'Say: my Salah and my sacrifice, and my living and my dying are all for Allah'?
options: A comprehensive outline of the straight path (Sirat-e-Mustaqeem), the soul of Islamic life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a comprehensive outline of the straight path. This verse teaches that every breath, every step and every deed of a Muslim is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and not for anyone else or for the desires of his own self.

mcqs.q: What command is given in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 208?
options: 'O believers! Spend your wealth openly only'
'O believers! Build houses near the mosque'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Enter Islam completely.' Among the requirements of Ibadat is that every sphere of life be brought within the circle of obedience to Allah: accepting all His commands, acting upon them, leaving the forbidden and fulfilling the obligatory.

mcqs.q: What is Taqwa, as explained in the lesson on worship?
options: A type of dress worn by scholars
A journey to a sacred place
A heartfelt condition by which the desire to do good deeds and hatred for evils is created
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a heartfelt condition creating desire for good and hatred for evil. Taqwa is the stage after purity of the heart, cleanliness of the soul and sincerity of action, and it is the stated purpose of Ibadat.

mcqs.q: Which qualities are created in a person by observing Salah, according to the effects of worship?
options: Punctuality, outward and inward purity, obedience to the leader and collectivity
mcqs.why: The correct answer is punctuality, purity, obedience to the leader and collectivity. The lesson states that by observing Salah these qualities are created in man, and he is also saved from immodesty and shamelessness.

mcqs.q: What effect does Zakat have on a person's heart, according to the lesson?
options: The love of wealth decreases, and he feels happiness in helping others financially
He stops working for a living
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the love of wealth decreases. Through Zakat, a believer's attachment to wealth weakens and he feels real happiness in financially helping people like himself, while Hajj teaches collectivity on a worldwide level and fasting creates Taqwa.

mcqs.q: What lesson does Hajj teach at the worldwide level?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the lesson of collectivity. Among the effects of Ibadat on general life, Hajj teaches believers from all over the world to gather as one community, while worship in general teaches living together with society and sacrificing personal interest for collective benefit.

mcqs.q: What is the key to the acceptance of Ibadat (worship)?
options: Performing worship in large quantity only
Performing worship at a famous place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is correctness of intention and sincerity. The effects of worship on a believer's life are attained on the basis of his intention and sincerity, and these two are the key to the acceptance of Ibadat by Allah Almighty.

lessons.title: Jihad (Introduction, Importance and Types)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Concept of Jihad

  • Jihad is an Arabic word derived from "Juhd".
  • Its literal meaning is: hard work, struggle, much effort and striving.
  • In Shariah terms: Every struggle and effort for the pleasure of Allah Almighty, which is for the exaltation, protection of the religion of Allah Almighty, and the protection and defence of the country and nation.
  • It is also every effort and struggle which is for the reform of society, to establish goodness and virtue, and to end evils and corruptions.

Virtue and Importance of Jihad

  • Islam has given great virtue and importance to Jihad, because ending killing, corruption, oppression and every kind of evil in the world, which becomes the cause of fitnah and corruption within society, and establishing an atmosphere of peace and security in the world, and protecting human rights, is possible only through Jihad.

Surah At-Tawbah: 41: وَجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ

  • Translation: And strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives; that is better for you, if you know.
  • Regarding Jihad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The person who died in such a state that in his life he neither practically performed Jihad nor desired Jihad, died at the level of hypocrisy. (Sahih Muslim: 1910)
  • Islam has also emphasised that the believer himself should remain firm on truth, speak the truth, and persuade others to remain firm on truth. Keeping striving for the exaltation of truth is called Afdal-ul-Jihad.

Hadith — the best Jihad (Sunan Abi Dawood: 4344): أَفْضَلُ الْجِهَادِ كَلِمَةُ عَدْلٍ عِنْدَ سُلْطَانٍ جَائِرٍ

  • Translation: The Holy Messenger ﷺ said: speaking a word of truth before a cruel ruler is the best Jihad.

Objectives of Jihad

  • The basic objectives of Jihad are: establishing an atmosphere of peace and security in the world, and protecting human rights.
  • Jihad fi Sabeelillah is that everything should be done only for the pleasure of Allah Almighty, so that the religion of Allah Almighty is established on His earth.
  • Special objective (a) — Punishment for breaking a treaty: Islam lays great emphasis on fulfilling treaties; the command has been given to fight that nation which makes a treaty with the Islamic government not to wage war, and then keeps warlike intentions behind that treaty.
  • Special objective (b) — Respect for humanity and help of the oppressed: Islam carries a very great message of human dignity; supporting and helping the oppressed, and freeing them from the oppression of the oppressors, has been declared obligatory for the Islamic government.
  • Special objective (c) — Ending fitnah and corruption: Among the basic objectives of Islamic teachings are restoring peace, spreading love and tolerance, and ending oppression, fitnah and corruption.

Kind 1 — Jihad Against the Desires of the Self

  • There are three kinds of Jihad; the first is Jihad against the desires of the self (nafs).
  • The inner power that stops man from the obedience and worship of Allah Almighty is his Nafs-e-Ammarah, which incites man towards sins, evils and disobedience: in which are self-liking, hatred, backbiting, lying and foul language, and the domination of other desires of the self, which can spoil man's deeds and character.
  • Keeping this Nafs-e-Ammarah under control comes under the category of Jihad.
  • The saying of Allah is: "And whoever fears standing before his Lord and restrains himself from the desire of his self, for him the everlasting abode is Paradise" (Surah An-Nazi'at: 40).

Hadith — the Mujahid (Sunan Tirmidhi: 1621): الْمُجَاهِدُ مَنْ جَاهَدَ نَفْسَهُ

  • Translation: The Mujahid is the one who strives against his self — the Holy Prophet ﷺ declared that person who controls his self a Mujahid.
  • In some narrations, Jihad with the self has been called Jihad-e-Akbar.

Kind 2 — Jihad to End Evils

  • When individual evils become common, they together take the form of collective corruption. Islam has named all these evils "Munkarat".
  • Munkarat includes oppression and excess, theft, gambling, behaviour based on verbal and national pride, false testimonies, stubbornness and bribery, adulteration, shortfall in weights and measures, corrupt customs, violation of the rights of the deserving, and usury, etc.
  • To end Munkarat and reform society, the Holy Quran has mentioned different ways: sometimes it has been named Amr bil-Ma'roof wa Nahi anil-Munkar, sometimes Dawah and Tableegh, and sometimes the advice of truth and patience.

Hadith — removing an evil (Sahih Muslim: 49): مَنْ رَأَى مِنْكُمْ مُنْكَرًا فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ بِيَدِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِلِسَانِهِ، فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَبِقَلْبِهِ

  • Translation: Whoever sees an evil, he should remove it with his hand; if he cannot remove it with his hand, then with his tongue; if he cannot do so even with his tongue, then he should consider it evil in his heart.

Kind 3 — Jihad bis-Saif / Armed Jihad (Qital)

  • Jihad bis-Saif means Jihad with the sword — that is, doing Jihad with weapons.
  • It means that if an enemy power attacks an Islamic country, then fighting for the protection of its borders and the religion, faith, life and wealth, honour and dignity of its citizens is obligatory upon that country.
  • For defence, Allah Almighty gave the Muslims permission for armed Jihad against those disbelievers.
  • The saying of Allah Almighty is: "Those Muslims who are fought against have permission to fight too, because they are being wronged. And Allah Almighty will help them, and indeed He is Able to help them" (Al-Hajj: 39).

Conditions of Armed Jihad

  • Islam has laid down some conditions for armed Jihad, keeping which in mind Jihad should be done:
  • (a) I'la-e-Kalimatullah (exaltation of the religion of Allah Almighty): The first condition of armed Jihad is that it should be only for the exaltation of the religion of Allah Almighty.
  • (b) Declaration by the Islamic state: The second condition of armed Jihad is that the declaration of Qital should be by the state. In Islam, only and only the state is authorised to declare Qital. The declaration or fatwa (for war) of any individual or group has no Shariah status; rather, such a declaration or fatwa comes under the category of "Fasad fil-Ard".
  • (c) Suitable military strength should be available: It is also a condition for armed Jihad that the Islamic government should have suitable strength and power to fight the opposing force. The Holy Quran emphasises keeping the Islamic state strong: "And prepare against them as much strength as you can, and ready horses, so that through it you may strike awe into the enemies of Allah Almighty and your enemies, and others besides them whom you do not know and Allah Almighty knows. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah Almighty, its reward will be given to you in full, and you will not be wronged even slightly."
  • (d) Ignorant ways should not be used in fighting: At the time of fighting, fight only those who are armed in opposition and keep trying to fight. Hands should not be raised against women, children, old people, the wounded and ordinary citizens. The dead of the enemy should not be mutilated. Fields, crops, houses and cattle should not be destroyed unnecessarily.

mcqs.q: From which word is 'Jihad' derived, and what is its literal meaning?
options: From 'Juhd'; it means hard work, struggle and striving
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Jihad comes from 'Juhd' and means hard work, struggle and striving. In Shariah terms, it is every struggle and effort made for the pleasure of Allah for the exaltation and protection of His religion and the defence of country and nation.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Abi Dawood (4344), what is the best Jihad (Afdal-ul-Jihad)?
options: Giving all one's wealth in charity
Speaking a word of truth before a cruel ruler
mcqs.why: The correct answer is speaking a word of truth before a cruel ruler. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared this the best Jihad, because remaining firm on truth and persuading others to remain firm on truth requires great courage.

mcqs.q: According to Sahih Muslim (1910), a person who died without practically performing Jihad and without even desiring it died upon what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a level of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah (PBUH) said that the person who died in such a state that he neither performed Jihad in his life nor desired it, died at the level of hypocrisy (Sahih Muslim, 1910).

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sunan Tirmidhi (1621), who is a Mujahid?
options: Only the one who fights with a sword
The one who leads every army
The one who owns war horses
The one who strives against his own self
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who strives against his own self. Controlling the Nafs-e-Ammarah, which incites man towards sins and disobedience, is itself Jihad, and in some narrations this Jihad against the self has been called Jihad-e-Akbar.

mcqs.q: What is the inner power that stops man from the obedience and worship of Allah and incites him towards sins called?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Nafs-e-Ammarah. It incites man towards sins, evils and disobedience, including self-liking, hatred, backbiting and lying, and keeping it under control comes under Jihad against the desires of the self.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sahih Muslim (49), if a person sees an evil and cannot remove it with his hand or his tongue, what should he do?
options: Consider it evil in his heart
Join the people doing the evil
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to consider it evil in his heart. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered that whoever sees an evil should remove it with his hand; if he cannot, then with his tongue; and if he cannot do even that, then he should consider it evil in his heart.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is counted among the Munkarat (evils) that Jihad against evils seeks to end?
options: Adulteration and shortfall in weights and measures
mcqs.why: The correct answer is adulteration and shortfall in weights and measures. Munkarat include oppression, theft, gambling, false testimonies, bribery, adulteration, short weights and measures, violation of rights and usury, all of which corrupt society.

mcqs.q: Who alone is authorised in Islam to declare armed Jihad (Qital)?
options: Any army commander on his own
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Islamic state. The declaration or fatwa of war by any individual or group has no Shariah status; rather, such a declaration comes under the category of Fasad fil-Ard (corruption in the land).

mcqs.q: During armed Jihad, against whom must hands NOT be raised, according to the conditions of fighting?
options: Women, children, old people, the wounded and ordinary citizens
Those who keep trying to fight
mcqs.why: The correct answer is women, children, old people, the wounded and ordinary citizens. Islam forbids ignorant ways in fighting: only those who are armed and fighting may be fought, the enemy dead must not be mutilated, and fields, crops, houses and cattle must not be destroyed unnecessarily.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Hajj, verse 39, why were the Muslims given permission to fight?
options: Because they had become the majority
Because their trade routes were closed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because they were being wronged. Allah gave permission for armed Jihad in defence to those Muslims who were fought against, because they were oppressed, and He promised to help them, for He is Able to help them.

lessons.title: Bi'that-e-Nabawi (PBUH) - The Advent of Prophethood
lessons.notes_html:
What is Ba'sat-e-Nabawi?

  • The blessed age of the Holy Prophet ﷺ had reached forty years.
  • He was engaged, as usual, in the solitude and worship of the cave of Hira in the month of Ramadan.
  • One day Jibraeel (AS) came to him by the command of Allah Almighty and illuminated the light of Prophethood hidden in his chest with the words of revelation, blessing him with Nubuwwat and Risalah.
  • This is Ba'sat-e-Nabvi.

The First Revelation (Al-'Alaq: 1-5)

First revelation: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ، اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ (1) خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ (2) اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ (3) الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ (4) عَلَّمَ الْإِنْسَانَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ (5)

  • Translation: (O Prophet!) Read in the name of your Sustainer who created (1). He created man from a clot of blood (2). Read; your Sustainer is the Most Generous (3). Who taught by the pen (4). He taught man what he did not know (5).
  • The first Surah revealed was Surah Al-'Alaq, and the first revelation came in Ramadan-ul-Mubarak.
  • The mention of reading and the pen in the first revelation shows that education and teaching stand at the centre of Ba'sat.

Signs (Aasar) of Ba'sat-e-Nabvi

  • An extraordinary event, contrary to habit, which appears at the hands of a Prophet after the announcement of Prophethood and points towards his Ba'sat is called a miracle, and is counted among the signs of Prophethood.
  • Six years before Ba'sat, the Holy Prophet ﷺ began to see a light and brightness, with no sound of any kind, seeing which he used to become extremely happy.
  • It is the law of Allah Almighty that when revelation begins upon a Prophet, first of all he is shown true dreams.
  • Hazrat Aisha (RA) narrated in Bukhari Sharif that the revelation upon the Holy Prophet ﷺ began with true dreams; the dreams he saw at night used to come true like the light of the morning.
  • Whenever he passed through the streets of Makkah Mukarramah, a voice used to come from the stones and trees:

Greeting of the stones and trees: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ

  • Translation: O Messenger of Allah! Peace be upon you. When he looked right and left, there used to be nothing except stones and trees.
  • He said: I recognise a stone in Makkah which used to greet me before Ba'sat (Sahih Muslim: 2277).

Conditions of Arabia Before Ba'sat

  • Makkah Mukarramah had become the big city of Arabia and the spiritual and social centre of the Quraysh, equal to Sanaa, the famous city of Yemen, in trade, civilisation, economy and progress.
  • The trade caravans of the Quraysh used to travel twice a year to Syria and Yemen, so the residents of Makkah were endowed with every facility of life.
  • In the fifth century AD, Qusayy bin Kilab — the grandfather in the fifth generation of the Holy Prophet ﷺ — made the administrative structure of Makkah, founded on unity, collective cooperation, general understanding and joint opinion.
  • For solving war, trade and other social matters, a consultative council named Dar-un-Nadwah was established.
  • Many families had become very rich; some gave charity and helped the needy, but others earned through usury and unlawful means, were pleasure-seekers, stubborn and hard-hearted towards the weak, and proud of their wealth and children.
  • They did not consider drinking, oppression, immorality, obscenity, gambling, theft and betting as bad; causing pain to neighbours, not caring for Silah Rahmi and unjust killing was their hobby.
  • They had become hard-hearted, dry-tempered and merciless, and used to take pride even in burying their own daughters alive.
  • Due to the prevalence of ignorance, idol-worship had become their religious sign; inside the Ka'batullah alone, three hundred and sixty idols were placed.

The condition of the world (Ar-Room: 41): ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ

  • Translation: Corruption had appeared on land and sea — defects had arisen in the beliefs and deeds of the religions and civilisations of the world.

Objectives of Ba'sat-e-Nabvi

  • The objectives of Ba'sat are education and teaching; Allah Almighty made four points its pivot and centre (Al-Jumu'ah: 2):
  • 1. Reciting and conveying the verses of Allah Almighty to them.
  • 2. Purifying those human beings.
  • 3. Teaching them the Book.
  • 4. Teaching them matters of wisdom.
  • That is, the Holy Prophet ﷺ was a preacher who recited the verses, a teacher who taught the verses, a guide who explained the verses, and a reformer who acted upon the verses.

mcqs.q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive Prophethood (Ba'sat) in the cave of Hira?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is forty years. When the blessed age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) reached forty years, Hazrat Jibraeel (AS) came to him in the cave of Hira in the month of Ramadan and blessed him with Nubuwwat and Risalah through the first revelation.

mcqs.q: Which was the first Surah revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Al-'Alaq. Its first five verses ('Read in the name of your Sustainer who created...') were the first revelation, and their mention of reading and the pen shows that education and teaching stand at the centre of Ba'sat.

mcqs.q: With what did the revelation upon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) begin, according to the narration of Hazrat Aisha (RA) in Bukhari?
options: A loud voice from the sky
mcqs.why: The correct answer is true dreams. Hazrat Aisha (RA) narrated that the revelation upon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) began with true dreams, and the dreams he saw at night used to come true like the light of the morning.

mcqs.q: What did the stones and trees of Makkah say when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed by, before Ba'sat?
options: 'Assalamu Alaika Ya Rasool Allah' (Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Assalamu Alaika Ya Rasool Allah.' Whenever he passed through the streets of Makkah, a voice of greeting used to come from the stones and trees, and he said: 'I recognise a stone in Makkah which used to greet me before Ba'sat' (Sahih Muslim, 2277).
