mcqs.q: Who founded the consultative council Dar-un-Nadwah in Makkah in the fifth century AD?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qusayy bin Kilab. He was the grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the fifth generation, who made the administrative structure of Makkah and established Dar-un-Nadwah for solving war, trade and other social matters by consultation.

mcqs.q: How many idols were placed inside the Ka'batullah before Ba'sat, according to the lesson?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three hundred and sixty. Due to the prevalence of ignorance, idol-worship had become the religious sign of the Arabs, and inside the Ka'batullah alone 360 idols were placed, alongside evils like usury, gambling and burying daughters alive.

mcqs.q: How often did the trade caravans of the Quraysh travel to Syria and Yemen?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is twice a year. The trade caravans of the Quraysh used to travel twice a year to Syria and Yemen, so the residents of Makkah were endowed with every facility of life and the city was a great centre of trade and civilisation.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Jumu'ah, verse 2, which four tasks form the pivot of Ba'sat-e-Nabvi?
options: Reciting the verses, purifying the people, teaching the Book and teaching wisdom
mcqs.why: The correct answer is reciting the verses, purification, teaching the Book and teaching wisdom. These four points of Surah Al-Jumu'ah, verse 2 are the objectives of Ba'sat: the Prophet (PBUH) was a preacher who recited the verses, a teacher, a guide and a reformer.

mcqs.q: What extraordinary sign did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) begin to see six years before Ba'sat?
options: A light and brightness, with no sound of any kind
Armies of angels in the sky
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a light and brightness without any sound. Six years before Ba'sat, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) began to see this light, seeing which he used to become extremely happy, and this was among the signs pointing towards his Prophethood.

mcqs.q: What is a miracle (mu'jizah), according to the lesson on Ba'sat?
options: A dream seen by an ordinary person
An extraordinary event, contrary to habit, which appears at the hands of a Prophet after the announcement of Prophethood
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an extraordinary event at the hands of a Prophet after the announcement of Prophethood. Such an event, contrary to habit, points towards his Ba'sat and is counted among the signs (Aasar) of Prophethood.

lessons.title: Dawah and Tabligh (Invitation and Preaching)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Concept of Dawah and Tableegh

  • In Arabic, the literal meaning of Dawah is calling and summoning, while the meaning of Tableegh is conveying.
  • In religious terminology, calling people towards Islam — calling towards all matters and religious education — is called Dawah-e-Deen.
  • Conveying its matters fully to other people, nations and countries with goodwill and zeal is called Tableegh.

Allah Almighty says (Fussilat: 33): وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا

  • Translation: And who can be better in speech than the one who calls towards Allah and does righteous deeds.

First Stage — Secret Tableegh

  • In the Makkan life of the Holy Prophet ﷺ there are two stages of Dawah and Tableegh.
  • The three years after Ba'sat were spent in preaching Tawheed with great silence and secrecy.
  • The first to accept Islam: among men Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), among women Hazrat Khadijah (RA), among slaves Zaid bin Harith (RA), and among children Hazrat Ali (RA).
  • Work was done first on close ones and neighbouring friends; gradually people kept entering Islam and a small group of Muslims was formed.
  • The house of Hazrat Arqam, near Mount Safa — Dar-e-Arqam — became their gathering place and centre, where they used to get the education of the Holy Quran and offer Salah.
  • At the time of the second revelation Allah Almighty said (Surah Al-Muddaththir: 1-3) — Translation: O one wrapped in the cloak of Prophethood (1), rise and then warn (2), and proclaim the greatness of your Sustainer (3).

Second Stage — Open and Public Tableegh

The command (Ash-Shu'ara: 214): وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الْأَقْرَبِينَ

  • Translation: (O Prophet!) Warn your close relatives.
  • After this command, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited the family of his grandfather Abdul Muttalib.
  • Then, after climbing Mount Safa, he conveyed the message of Allah Almighty to the people, neighbours and the people of Makkah, and was commanded to make Dawah general — to invite the whole nation.
  • The Quran was sent through Arabic revelation so that he may warn the people of Makkah and the people around them (Surah Ash-Shura: 7).

For all mankind (Saba: 28): وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا كَافَّةً لِلنَّاسِ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا

  • Translation: And (O Prophet), We sent you as a bearer of good news and a warner for all human beings — giving Dawah an international status.

Principles of Dawah and Tableegh

The Divine command (Surah An-Nahl: 125): ادْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ وَجَادِلْهُمْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ

  • Translation: Call to the way of your Sustainer with wisdom and good advice. And debate with them in a manner which is the best.
  • 1. Wisdom (Hikmah): conversation is held according to the environment and understanding of the audience; understanding his mental ability, Dawah is done with suitable scholarly and rational arguments according to circumstances, occasion and place.
  • 2. Good advice (Mau'izah Hasanah): stating goodness and evil before the audience in an effective, advising manner, in which his heart is not hurt, but he is convinced for the truth by talking in a good manner.
  • 3. Debate in the best manner: if a situation of debate arises, conversation should be held with strong arguments in a better and soft tone, with understanding and explaining; anger, excitement and bitter conversation should be avoided.
  • For the one who does Dawah and Tableegh, it is also necessary that he himself should act upon the matter which he preaches to others.
  • Hearing the criticism of the audience, the Da'i (preacher) should overlook it, not take revenge, quarrel or become angry.

Objectives of Dawah and Tableegh

  • The message of Allah Almighty should be conveyed to people.
  • Allah Almighty should be believed as One Allah and Lord; no one should be made a partner with Him in His Being, attributes, powers and rights.
  • Considering Islam as the true religion, one should consider oneself answerable before Allah Almighty.
  • Believing in the Prophets of Allah Almighty, they should be followed and obeyed.
  • Considering Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the Seal of the Prophets, as the last Prophet and acting upon his Seerah, goodness should be promoted and encouragement given to end evils.

Effects of Dawah and Tableegh

  • Suwaid bin Samit, an Ansari of Madinah famous for bravery and poetry, came to Makkah in the Hajj season and, hearing some verses of the Holy Quran from the blessed tongue of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, became convinced of the truth of Islam.
  • His inclination affected the people of Yathrib, and within three years a large number of the people of Madinah Munawwarah entered Islam.
  • Then the migration of the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah began; the Muslims became powerful, and the Holy Prophet ﷺ also migrated to Madinah.
  • There he laid the foundation of a mosque and made peace and reconciliation treaties with the tribes of Madinah and its surroundings.
  • After Ghazwa Badr, Ghazwa Uhud, Ghazwa Khandaq and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, he wrote preaching letters to kings, and Khaybar was conquered.
  • After that, truth triumphed and falsehood was defeated — Makkah Mukarramah was conquered.
  • As a result of Dawah and Tableegh, on the occasion of Hajjat-ul-Wida, more than one hundred thousand Companions (RA) were ready for Hajj.

mcqs.q: What are the literal meanings of Dawah and Tableegh?
options: Dawah means writing; Tableegh means reading
Dawah means calling and summoning; Tableegh means conveying
Dawah means travelling; Tableegh means staying
Dawah means debating; Tableegh means deciding
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Dawah means calling and summoning, while Tableegh means conveying. In religious terminology, calling people towards Islam is Dawah-e-Deen, and conveying its matters fully to other people and nations with goodwill and zeal is Tableegh.

mcqs.q: For how long did the first stage of Dawah, the secret Tableegh, continue after Ba'sat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three years. The three years after Ba'sat were spent in preaching Tawheed with great silence and secrecy, working first on close ones and neighbouring friends, until a small group of Muslims was formed.

mcqs.q: Who was the first person among men to accept Islam during the secret Tableegh?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). The first to accept Islam were: among men Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), among women Hazrat Khadijah (RA), among slaves Hazrat Zaid bin Harith (RA), and among children Hazrat Ali (RA).

mcqs.q: What was Dar-e-Arqam, the house of Hazrat Arqam near Mount Safa?
options: The house of the chief of Quraysh
The gathering place and centre of the early Muslims, where they learnt the Quran and offered Salah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the gathering place and centre of the early Muslims. At Dar-e-Arqam, near Mount Safa, the small group of Muslims used to gather to receive the education of the Holy Quran and to offer Salah during the secret stage of Dawah.

mcqs.q: Which command began the second stage of open and public Tableegh?
options: Surah Ash-Shu'ara, verse 214: 'Warn your close relatives'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Surah Ash-Shu'ara, verse 214, 'Warn your close relatives.' After this command, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) invited the family of Abdul Muttalib and then, climbing Mount Safa, conveyed Allah's message openly to the people of Makkah.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Saba, verse 28, for whom was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent as a bearer of good news and a warner?
options: Only for the people of Arabia
Only for the people of Makkah and Madinah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is for all mankind. Surah Saba, verse 28 gave Dawah an international status: the Prophet (PBUH) was sent as Bashir (bearer of good news) and Nazeer (warner) for all human beings, not for one nation only.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nahl, verse 125, what are the three principles of Dawah and Tableegh?
options: Wisdom (Hikmah), good advice (Mau'izah Hasanah) and debate in the best manner
mcqs.why: The correct answer is wisdom, good advice and debate in the best manner. The Da'i must speak according to the audience's understanding, advise in a way that does not hurt the heart, and if debate arises, argue softly with strong arguments, avoiding anger and bitter words.

mcqs.q: What is required of the Da'i (the one who does Dawah) regarding his own practice?
options: He must preach only and not act
He must take revenge on critics
He must become angry at opposition
He must himself act upon what he preaches to others
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he must himself act upon what he preaches. It is also necessary for the Da'i to overlook the criticism of the audience and not take revenge, quarrel or become angry, following the principles of Dawah given in Surah An-Nahl, verse 125.

mcqs.q: Who was Suwaid bin Samit, whose acceptance of Islam affected the people of Yathrib (Madinah)?
options: An Ansari of Madinah famous for bravery and poetry, who heard verses of the Quran from the Prophet (PBUH) in the Hajj season
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an Ansari of Madinah famous for bravery and poetry. Suwaid bin Samit came to Makkah in the Hajj season, heard some verses of the Holy Quran from the blessed tongue of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), became convinced of the truth of Islam, and within three years a large number of Madinans entered Islam.

mcqs.q: How many Companions (RA) were present with the Holy Prophet (PBUH) on the occasion of Hajjat-ul-Wida, as a result of Dawah and Tableegh?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is more than one hundred thousand. As a result of Dawah and Tableegh, by the time of Hajjat-ul-Wida more than one lakh Companions (RA) were ready for Hajj with the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after the conquests of Khaybar and Makkah.

lessons.title: Hijrat-e-Madina and Ghazwat (Battles)
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Concept of Hijrah

  • In Arabic, the meaning of Hijrah is separation, parting, and leaving one place forever and going to another place — that is, migrating for the sake of religion.
  • In Islam, Hijrah is: for the attainment of the pleasure of Allah Almighty, leaving one's original homeland and relatives and adopting residence in another country, especially when people are subjugated and oppressed.
  • If they have difficulties in acting upon Islam and living life, they should migrate to a place where the acts of worship of the religion and household works can be done, and acting upon them is easy.

Causes of the Migration to Madinah

  • Oppression upon the Muslims: in Makkah the enemies oppressed every person who accepted Islam, leaving no opportunity to give physical and mental pains; they locked up the Holy Prophet ﷺ and other Muslims for three years in Shi'b-e-Abi Talib and boycotted them, and martyred several Companions (RA).
  • Restriction on the Dawah of Islam in Makkah: before Ba'sat the Quraysh used to call the Holy Prophet ﷺ by the titles of Sadiq and Ameen, but after the announcement of his Prophethood they became his mortal enemies, so inviting people to Islam became extremely difficult.
  • The encouraging experience of the migration to Abyssinia: troubled by the harsh behaviour of the Quraysh, a few Companions (RA) migrated to Abyssinia, where they got satisfaction and comfort, though they later returned due to the conspiracies of the opponents.
  • The eagerness of the people of Madinah: some righteous people of Madinah had pledged allegiance (Bay'at) twice at Aqabah and desired that the Holy Prophet ﷺ should come to Yathrib and teach them the matters of the religion.
  • Divine command: on 27 Safar in the fourteenth year of Ba'sat, the Holy Prophet ﷺ gave the Muslims permission to migrate towards Yathrib, and people kept leaving secretly; this migration was obligatory upon all Muslims.
  • On one side the excesses of the polytheists in Makkah were extremely great; on the other side, due to the general popularity of Islam in Yathrib, the environment was favourable for the Muslims.

The Event of Hijrah

  • Consultation of the disbelievers in Dar-un-Nadwah: when the polytheists of Makkah saw the Muslims living in peace in Madinah, with powerful tribes like Aws and Khazraj as their supporters, they became worried due to jealousy and gathered in Dar-un-Nadwah to plan against the Holy Prophet ﷺ; Allah Almighty had already informed him of this plot.
  • Trusts returned: despite the severe enmity of the disbelievers, he seated Hazrat Ali (RA) on his bed so that the trusts of the disbelievers kept with him could be delivered safely to their owners.
  • Taking Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) with him, he left Makkah Mukarramah, addressing it: You are very pure and beloved to me, but if my nation had not forced me to leave from here, I would not have gone to any place other than you.
  • Stay in the cave of Thawr: the Holy Prophet ﷺ and Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) stayed inside the cave of Thawr for three days.
  • Departure to Madinah: on the fourth day he came out of the cave and took Abdullah bin Uraiqit with him on hire to show the way.
  • Arrival in Quba: he reached the village of Quba in the year 14 of Prophethood, corresponding to the year 1 Hijri; he rested there for a few days, built a mosque and offered Salah in it, which is called Masjid-e-Quba — the mosque whose foundation was laid on piety from the first day.
  • Entry into Madinah Munawwarah: on Friday he set out towards Madinah; reaching the village of Banu Salim bin Awf, he led the Friday Salah in the valley of Batan, and on reaching Madinah the people of Madinah gave him an enthusiastic welcome.

Virtue of Hijrah

  • The Muslims who migrate get the benefit of this world and the Hereafter; they are deserving of the mercy of Allah Almighty, and for them forgiveness, Paradise and the best of rewards are kept, with the assurance that their deeds will not be wasted (Aal-e-Imran: 195).
  • Until Jihad became obligatory, the greatest deed at that time was Hijrah.
  • After the Conquest of Makkah, Hijrah is not obligatory but recommended (Mustahab), on the condition that it should be in the way of Allah Almighty, for remaining firm on the religion, and for its Dawah and propagation.

Ghazwah — Meaning

  • The meaning of Ghazwah is going out to fight someone, attacking, and waging war.
  • According to Muhadditheen and Seerah writers, a Ghazwah is that military expedition in which the Holy Prophet ﷺ himself participated, striving for the exaltation of the word of Allah as the commander of the army.

The Important Ghazwat

  • Ghazwa Badr: Ramadan, 2 Hijri — the polytheists of Makkah, under the leadership of Abu Jahl, intended to attack Madinah; the Holy Prophet ﷺ confronted them near the field of Badr and Allah Almighty granted victory to the Muslims. The Muslims were 313 and the disbelievers 1000; 70 disbelievers were killed and 70 made prisoners.
  • Ghazwa Uhud: Shawwal, 3 Hijri — one year after Badr, the polytheists under Abu Sufyan attacked Madinah and were confronted at Uhud; the Muslims suffered great loss, but the enemy also did not succeed in its objectives. Uhud is the second Ghazwah.
  • Ghazwa Khandaq: Dhu-ul-Qa'dah, 5 Hijri — the polytheists and disbelievers of all Arabia together attacked Madinah with great force; its other name is Ghazwa Ahzab. Allah Almighty sent a storm and severe wind and ruined the intentions of the disbelievers.
  • Ghazwa Khaybar: 7 Hijri — the Jews of Khaybar started a severe rebellion; all their forts were conquered, and the last, strong fort Qamoos was conquered under the leadership of Sher-e-Khuda Haider-e-Karrar Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).
  • Conquest of Makkah: the Muslims conquered Makkah Mukarramah in Ramadan-ul-Mubarak, 8 Hijri.
  • Ghazwa Hunayn: 8 Hijri, after the Conquest of Makkah; in this battle the Muslims got success.
  • Ghazwa Tabuk: 9 Hijri — on the information that the Romans and their allies had set out to fight the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with his Mujahideen towards Tabuk; when the Romans saw the determination of the Muslims, they went back, and the Islamic army returned without fighting.

mcqs.q: For how long were the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the Muslims boycotted in Shi'b-e-Abi Talib?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three years. Among the causes of the Hijrah, the enemies of Islam locked up the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and other Muslims for three years in Shi'b-e-Abi Talib and boycotted them, alongside other severe oppression in Makkah.

mcqs.q: On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) give the Muslims permission to migrate towards Yathrib (Madinah)?
options: 27 Safar, in the fourteenth year of Ba'sat
1 Muharram, in the tenth year of Ba'sat
12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, in the fifth year of Ba'sat
27 Rajab, in the first year of Hijrah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 27 Safar in the fourteenth year of Ba'sat. By Divine command, the Prophet (PBUH) permitted the migration to Yathrib, people kept leaving secretly, and at that time this migration was obligatory upon all Muslims.

mcqs.q: For how many days did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) stay in the cave of Thawr?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three days. Leaving Makkah with Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stayed inside the cave of Thawr for three days, and on the fourth day he set out for Madinah with the hired guide Abdullah bin Uraiqit.

mcqs.q: Who was hired to show the way during the journey of Hijrah to Madinah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Abdullah bin Uraiqit. On the fourth day, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) came out of the cave of Thawr and took Abdullah bin Uraiqit with him on hire to show the way to Madinah.

mcqs.q: Which mosque, built during the stay at Quba, is described as the mosque whose foundation was laid on piety from the first day?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Masjid-e-Quba. Reaching the village of Quba in 1 Hijri, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) rested there for a few days, built a mosque and offered Salah in it; it is the mosque whose foundation was laid on piety from the first day.

mcqs.q: What is the status of Hijrah after the Conquest of Makkah?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Hijrah is Mustahab (recommended) after the Conquest of Makkah, not obligatory. Until Jihad became obligatory, Hijrah was the greatest deed; afterwards it remains recommended when done in the way of Allah for remaining firm on the religion.

mcqs.q: According to the Muhadditheen and Seerah writers, what is a Ghazwah?
options: Any battle fought by the Muslims
A battle in which only the Ansar fought
A military expedition in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself participated as commander of the army
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an expedition in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself participated. Such an expedition, in which he strove for the exaltation of the word of Allah as commander of the army, is called a Ghazwah.

mcqs.q: What were the numbers of the two armies at Ghazwa Badr (Ramadan, 2 Hijri), and what was the result for the disbelievers?
options: Muslims 313 against 1000 disbelievers; 70 disbelievers were killed and 70 made prisoners
Muslims 1000 against 313 disbelievers; 70 Muslims were made prisoners
Muslims 700 against 700 disbelievers; no one was killed
Muslims 313 against 3000 disbelievers; 300 were made prisoners
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 313 Muslims against 1000 disbelievers, with 70 disbelievers killed and 70 made prisoners. At Badr the polytheists under Abu Jahl intended to attack Madinah, and Allah Almighty granted victory to the Muslims.

mcqs.q: By what other name is Ghazwa Khandaq (5 Hijri) known?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ghazwa Ahzab. In Dhu-ul-Qa'dah, 5 Hijri, the polytheists and disbelievers of all Arabia together (the Ahzab, confederate parties) attacked Madinah with great force, and Allah ruined their intentions by sending a storm and severe wind.

mcqs.q: Under whose leadership was the last and strong fort of Khaybar, Qamoos, conquered in 7 Hijri?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Ali (RA). At Ghazwa Khaybar in 7 Hijri, all the forts of the Jews of Khaybar were conquered, and the last, strong fort Qamoos was conquered under the leadership of Sher-e-Khuda Haider-e-Karrar Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).

lessons.title: Khasail and Shamail-e-Nabawi (PBUH)
lessons.notes_html:
What is Meant by Khasail and Shamail?

  • By Khasa'il and Shama'il of the Holy Prophet ﷺ are meant his excellent habits and characteristics.
  • Khasa'il means habit, and Shama'il means good nature, excellent habit and virtuous quality.
  • They include his outward excellences, inward characteristics and excellent habits: his day and night life (rising, sitting, eating, drinking, sleeping, waking), temperament, social life, dress, morals and pure characteristics.
  • They also include his behaviour with family members, meeting people, behaviour with companions, and his outward appearance, Seerah, blessed features and physical build.

Importance and Virtue of Khasail and Shamail

  • The pure life of the Holy Prophet ﷺ itself is the correct and complete picture of Islam.
  • Following his sayings and actions and his blessed life is the means of salvation for the believer.

An excellent model (Al-Ahzab: 21): لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ

  • Translation: (O Muslims!) In reality, for you there is an excellent model in the Messenger of Allah.
  • Allah Almighty made the Messenger ﷺ a collection of excellent habits — an unparalleled form of exalted Seerah, high morals and excellent qualities.

Exalted morals (Surah Al-Qalam: 4): وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ

  • Translation: Indeed, your morals are exalted — the Quran itself bore witness to his morals.
  • He ﷺ was the most courteous, the most well-mannered, the most truthful and generous, the most righteous in deeds, the most bound by promise, and the most trustworthy of all.
  • Those who want to make their life of solitude or togetherness good and successful should follow the Khasa'il and Shama'il of the Holy Prophet ﷺ with complete willingness.

His Way of Helping Others

  • His ﷺ way was one of sympathy and goodwill: doing Silah Rahmi, carrying the burdens of the helpless, helping the empty-handed, honouring the guest, and helping in the calamities that come in the path of truth (as Hazrat Khadijah (RA) said).
  • Listening to the cries of the oppressed and widows and helping them was his favourite occupation; for example, to get a stranger's loan recovered from Abu Jahl, he stood up, postponing his worship.
  • Doing good even to the enemy is among his blessed Khasa'il: when he went to the Jewish boy, he invited him to Islam.
  • On the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, instead of taking revenge for years of oppression and excesses, he forgave the hundreds of people of his nation and announced: Today there is no blame upon you; go, you are all free.

Household Engagements

  • Hazrat Aisha (RA) states that the Holy Prophet ﷺ used to clean his clothes himself, milk the goat himself, do his own work himself, and stitch (mend) his own clothes himself.
  • Hazrat Anas (RA) states that he never saw any person more kind and merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
  • He used to behave with family members cheerfully, fulfil their needs, and greet family members with salaam upon entering the house.

Behaviour with Neighbours — The Lesson

  • His blessed life teaches good conduct with neighbours and neighbourhood people, and taking care of their needs.
  • Sending them gifts and presents, visiting the sick (Iyadat), condoling, and inviting one another.
  • Helping the weak people of society, and doing good even to the enemy.

Khasail and Shamail in the Present Environment

  • Classroom: behaving with respect and gentleness with the teacher and classmates.
  • School: taking care of cleanliness and discipline.
  • Home: serving parents and helping in household work.
  • Neighbourhood: taking care of the needs of neighbours and taking the lead in salaam.
  • Playground: honesty and cooperation with companions.
  • City: taking care of cleanliness and respecting the rights of others.

mcqs.q: What do the words Khasa'il and Shama'il mean?
options: Khasa'il means habit, and Shama'il means good nature, excellent habit and virtuous quality
Khasa'il means battles, and Shama'il means journeys
Khasa'il means clothes, and Shama'il means food
Khasa'il means miracles, and Shama'il means dreams
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Khasa'il means habit and Shama'il means good nature and virtuous quality. The Khasa'il and Shama'il of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) include his day and night life, temperament, social life, dress, morals, outward appearance and pure characteristics.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Quran itself say about the morals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in Surah Al-Qalam, verse 4?
options: 'Indeed, you were sent to the Arabs'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Indeed, your morals are exalted' (Khuluqin Azeem). The Quran itself bore witness to the morals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who was the most courteous, truthful, generous, promise-bound and trustworthy of all people.

mcqs.q: According to Hazrat Khadijah (RA), which of the following was the way of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in helping others?
options: Carrying the burdens of the helpless
Waiting for people to ask many times
mcqs.why: The correct answer is carrying the burdens of the helpless. As Hazrat Khadijah (RA) described, his way was sympathy and goodwill: doing Silah Rahmi, carrying the burdens of the helpless, helping the empty-handed, honouring the guest and helping in calamities in the path of truth.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) announce for the people of Makkah on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah?
options: 'Today there is no blame upon you; go, you are all free'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Today there is no blame upon you; go, you are all free.' Instead of taking revenge for years of oppression and excesses, he forgave the hundreds of people of his nation, and doing good even to the enemy is among his blessed Khasa'il.

mcqs.q: According to Hazrat Aisha (RA), how did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) manage his personal household work?
options: He cleaned his clothes himself, milked the goat himself and stitched (mended) his own clothes himself
He always ordered servants to do everything
He never took part in household work
He left all work to the Companions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he did his own work himself. Hazrat Aisha (RA) states that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) used to clean his clothes himself, milk the goat himself, do his own work himself and mend his own clothes himself.

mcqs.q: What did Hazrat Anas (RA) say about the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and his family?
options: He was strict and distant with his family
He spent little time with his family
He never saw any person more kind and merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah (PBUH)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that no one was more kind and merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah (PBUH). Hazrat Anas (RA) testified to this, and the Prophet (PBUH) behaved cheerfully with family members, fulfilled their needs and greeted them with salaam on entering the house.

mcqs.q: How did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) do good even to his enemy, in the incident of the Jewish boy?
options: He gave him a large sum of money
He appointed him to a post
He freed him from a tax
He went to the Jewish boy and invited him to Islam
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he went to the Jewish boy and invited him to Islam. Doing good even to the enemy is among the blessed Khasa'il of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), just as helping the oppressed and widows was his favourite occupation.

mcqs.q: For whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stand up, postponing his worship, in order to help?
options: To receive a delegation of traders
To get a stranger's loan recovered from Abu Jahl
To settle his own business matter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to get a stranger's loan recovered from Abu Jahl. Listening to the cries of the oppressed and widows and helping them was his favourite occupation, and for this stranger's right he stood up, postponing his worship.

mcqs.q: What does the blessed life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) teach about neighbours?
options: Sending them gifts, visiting the sick (Iyadat), condoling and inviting one another
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sending gifts, visiting the sick, condoling and inviting one another. His life teaches good conduct with neighbours and taking care of their needs, along with helping the weak people of society.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) do upon entering his house?
options: He greeted the family members with salaam
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he greeted the family members with salaam upon entering the house. He behaved with them cheerfully and fulfilled their needs, and Hazrat Anas (RA) said he never saw anyone kinder and more merciful to his family than the Messenger of Allah (PBUH).

lessons.title: Manaqib-e-Ahl-e-Bait Athaar
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning and Concept of Manaqib

  • Manaqib is an Arabic word, whose singular is Manqabah, which means: praise, goodness, excellence and virtue.
  • In technical terms, the deeds and virtues of a famous personality are called Manqabah, whether in prose or in poetry.

Who are the Ahl-e-Bayt?

  • The literal meaning of Ahl-e-Bayt is household members: Ahl in Arabic means members/people, and Bayt means house.
  • In the terminology of the Holy Quran, by Ahl-e-Bayt is meant the household of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, which includes his pure family (Aal-e-Pak), his pure wives, and his children.

Hadith-e-Kisa — The People of the Cloak

  • It is narrated from Hazrat Aisha Siddiqua (RA) that the Holy Prophet ﷺ once called Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (may Allah be pleased with them all) and entered them under a cloak.

His dua for them (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 3871): اَللَّهُمَّ هَؤُلَاءِ أَهْلُ بَيْتِي فَأَذْهِبْ عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْسَ وَطَهِّرْهُمْ تَطْهِيرًا

  • Translation: O my Allah! These are my Ahl-e-Bayt. Remove impurity from them and purify them.
  • These four — Fatimah-uz-Zahra, Ali, Hasan and Husain (RA) — are the Ahl-e-Bayt-e-Athar named in the light of Hadith-e-Kisa, which is also linked with Ayat-e-Tatheer.

Love and Devotion for the Ahl-e-Bayt

  • Hadith-e-Thaqalayn: I leave two things with you; as long as you hold them firmly, you will not go astray: the Book of Allah Almighty and my Ahl-e-Bayt (Sunan Tirmidhi: 3786).
  • About Hazrat Fatimah (RA) he said: Fatimah is a part of my body; whoever angered her, angered me (Sahih Al-Bukhari: 3093).
  • For Hazrat Imam Hasan and Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) he said: These two are my sons; O Allah! I love them, You too love them, and love the one who loves them (Sunan Tirmidhi: 3775).
  • From these ahadith, the deep love and devotion of the Holy Prophet ﷺ for his Ahl-e-Bayt is evident.
  • Scholars have declared the love and honour of Ahl-e-Bayt equal to the love and honour of the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

Ummahat-ul-Mu'mineen

The Quran declares (Surah Al-Ahzab: 6): وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ

  • Translation: And the pure wives of the Holy Prophet ﷺ are the mothers of the believers.
  • The Holy Quran called his pure wives Ummahat-ul-Mu'mineen (mothers of the believers); their number is eleven.
  • Hazrat Khadijah-ul-Kubra (RA) — the first wife, the first to bring faith.
  • Hazrat Aisha Siddiqua (RA) — the daughter of Abu Bakr Siddique, a great woman jurist.
  • Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA) — Umm-ul-Masakeen; and Hazrat Zainab bint Jahsh (RA).
  • The rest: Hazrat Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Hazrat Hafsah bint Umar, Hazrat Umm-e-Salamah, Hazrat Juwairiyah bint Al-Harith, Hazrat Umm-e-Habibah (Ramlah bint Abu Sufyan), Hazrat Safiyyah bint Huyayy, Hazrat Maymunah bint Harith and Hazrat Mariyah Qibtiyyah (RA).
  • All of them are the mothers of the Ummah and the bright lights of guidance.

Four Rights of Ahl-e-Bayt

  • 1. They should be loved.
  • 2. These respected persons should be obeyed.
  • 3. The belief should be kept that they are just (Adil).
  • 4. Those who love them should be loved, and those who hate them should be hated.

mcqs.q: What is the singular of 'Manaqib', and what does it mean?
options: Manqabah; it means praise, goodness, excellence and virtue
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Manqabah, meaning praise, goodness, excellence and virtue. In technical terms, the deeds and virtues of a famous personality, whether expressed in prose or in poetry, are called Manqabah.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Ahl-e-Bayt?
options: Household members (Ahl means members/people, and Bayt means house)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is household members. In the terminology of the Holy Quran, by Ahl-e-Bayt is meant the household of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), which includes his pure family (Aal-e-Pak), his pure wives and his children.

mcqs.q: In Hadith-e-Kisa, which four personalities did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gather under his cloak and pray for?
options: Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra, Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (RA)
Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA)
Hazrat Hamza, Hazrat Abbas, Hazrat Jafar and Hazrat Aqeel (RA)
Hazrat Bilal, Hazrat Salman, Hazrat Abu Zar and Hazrat Miqdad (RA)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Fatimah-uz-Zahra, Ali, Hasan and Husain (may Allah be pleased with them all). As narrated by Hazrat Aisha (RA), the Prophet (PBUH) entered them under a cloak and prayed: 'O Allah! These are my Ahl-e-Bayt; remove impurity from them and purify them' (Sunan Tirmidhi, 3871), and this is linked with Ayat-e-Tatheer.

mcqs.q: According to Hadith-e-Thaqalayn, which two things did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) leave with the Ummah, holding firmly to which they will not go astray?
options: The Sunnah and the consensus of scholars
The Book of Allah and his Ahl-e-Bayt
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Book of Allah and his Ahl-e-Bayt. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'I leave two things with you; as long as you hold them firmly, you will not go astray: the Book of Allah Almighty and my Ahl-e-Bayt' (Sunan Tirmidhi, 3786).

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about Hazrat Fatimah (RA) in Sahih Al-Bukhari (3093)?
options: 'Fatimah is the chief of the Ansar'
'Fatimah is a part of my body; whoever angered her, angered me'
'Fatimah is the mother of the scholars'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Fatimah is a part of my body; whoever angered her, angered me.' This hadith, along with his words about Hasan and Husain, shows the deep love and devotion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for his Ahl-e-Bayt.

mcqs.q: By which title does the Holy Quran address the pure wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), and how many were they?
options: Ummahat-ul-Mu'mineen (mothers of the believers); they were eleven
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ummahat-ul-Mu'mineen, and they were eleven. Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 6 declares: 'And his pure wives are the mothers of the believers,' and all of them are the mothers of the Ummah and bright lights of guidance.

mcqs.q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the first person to bring faith?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Khadijah-ul-Kubra (RA). She was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the first to bring faith, while Hazrat Aisha Siddiqua (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) and a great woman jurist.

mcqs.q: Which of the pure wives was known by the title 'Umm-ul-Masakeen' (Mother of the Poor)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA). Among the eleven Ummahat-ul-Mu'mineen, she was famous for her generosity to the poor, which earned her the title Umm-ul-Masakeen, the Mother of the Poor.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is one of the four rights of the Ahl-e-Bayt upon us?
options: To keep the belief that they are just (Adil)
To give them our Zakat every year
To visit their graves every month
To name all our children after them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to keep the belief that they are just (Adil). The four rights of the Ahl-e-Bayt are: they should be loved; they should be obeyed; the belief should be kept that they are just; and those who love them should be loved while those who hate them should be hated.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (RA) in Sunan Tirmidhi (3775)?
options: 'These two are the chiefs of the Ansar'
'These two will lead the armies of Islam'
'These two are my sons; O Allah! I love them, You too love them, and love the one who loves them'
'These two are the most learned of the Ummah'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'These two are my sons; O Allah! I love them, You too love them, and love the one who loves them.' Scholars have declared that the love and honour of the Ahl-e-Bayt is equal to the love and honour of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself.

lessons.title: Manaqib-e-Sahaba Karam and Ashra Mubashra
lessons.notes_html:
Literal and Technical Meaning of Sahabi

  • Sahabi is derived from the Arabic word Suhbah, whose literal meaning is friendship.
  • In technical terms, a Sahabi is that personality who met the Holy Prophet ﷺ in the state of faith, and died with the safety of faith.

Manaqib (Virtues) of the Companions (RA)

  • Due to the blessed love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, these great personalities reached such a high station that none of the later ones can reach their rank.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: The best era is that of my era (Bukhari: 3651).
  • Through the Companions (RA), the Quran and Sunnah and the whole religion reached us; through their sacrifices, the religion of Islam reached every corner of the world.
  • It is obligatory for a Muslim to keep love for the Companions (RA) and keep honour and respect for them in the heart.
  • Allah Almighty said: The Muhajireen and Ansar who were foremost in bringing faith, and those who followed them in goodness — Allah Almighty is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him; He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which they will remain forever, and this is the great success (Surah At-Tawbah: 100).
  • Keeping heartfelt love and devotion for this pure group is exactly faith, whereas showing even a little disrespect and insolence in their honour is a great sin.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: Do not speak ill of my Companions, for if any one of you gives charity equal to Mount Uhud in gold, it still will not reach even one Mudd of theirs (Bukhari: 3673, Muslim: 222).

More Virtues of the Companions

Glad tidings (Mizan-ul-I'tidal by Adh-Dhahabi, Vol. 1, p. 422): طُوبَىٰ لِمَنْ رَآنِي وَآمَنَ بِي

  • Translation: Great glad tidings for the person who saw me and believed in me, and also for the one who saw such a person who had seen me — in this hadith, glad tidings have been given to the Companion and the Tabi'i.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: The best people among you are those of my era, then those who come after them, then those who come after them (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 6695).
  • Allah Almighty is pleased with the Ansar and Muhajireen, and He has prepared gardens of Paradise for them (Surah At-Tawbah: 100).
  • These personalities attained the honour of being Companions, and they hold the highest glory and exalted rank among all other human beings on the face of the earth, after the Prophets (AS).

Ashra Mubashra — Meaning

  • In Arabic, Ashrah means ten.
  • Mubashsharah is derived from the word Basharah, which means to give glad tidings.
  • So Ashra Mubashra are the ten human beings given glad tidings — the ten Companions to whom the Holy Prophet ﷺ gave the glad tidings of Paradise in this world itself.

Names of the Ashra Mubashra

  • Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique, Hazrat Umar Farooq, Hazrat Usman Ghani, Hazrat Ali Al-Murtaza (RA).
  • Hazrat Talhah, Hazrat Zubayr, Hazrat Abdur Rahman bin Awf (RA).
  • Hazrat Sa'd, Hazrat Sa'eed and Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA). (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 3747)

Lessons from the Companions for Daily Life

  • Adopt the truthfulness, trustworthiness, sacrifice and obedience to the Messenger ﷺ of the Companions in one's own life.
  • Learn lessons from the patience, justice and service to creation of the Ashrah Mubashsharah.
  • Keep the love and respect of the Companions in the heart.

mcqs.q: From which Arabic word is 'Sahabi' derived, and what is its literal meaning?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Suhbah', meaning friendship. In technical terms, a Sahabi is that personality who met the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the state of faith and died with the safety of faith.

mcqs.q: In technical terms, who is a Sahabi?
options: Anyone who lived in Madinah at that time
One who met the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the state of faith and died with the safety of faith
Only the close relatives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Anyone who heard a hadith from a Companion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one who met the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in the state of faith and died with faith. Through these blessed Companions, the Quran, the Sunnah and the whole religion reached us, and through their sacrifices Islam reached every corner of the world.

mcqs.q: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about his own era in Sahih Al-Bukhari (3651)?
options: 'The best era is the era of the Tabi'een'
'The best era is that of my era'
'The best era will be the last era'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'The best era is that of my era.' The Holy Prophet (PBUH) also said that the best people are those of his era, then those who come after them, then those who come after them (Sahih Bukhari, 6695).

mcqs.q: According to Surah At-Tawbah, verse 100, what has Allah prepared for the foremost Muhajireen and Ansar and those who followed them in goodness?
options: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which they will remain forever
Palaces of gold in this world
mcqs.why: The correct answer is gardens beneath which rivers flow, forever. Surah At-Tawbah, verse 100 declares that Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and this is described as the great success.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith (Bukhari 3673, Muslim 222), even charity equal to Mount Uhud in gold cannot reach what small amount given by a Companion?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one Mudd of theirs. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) forbade speaking ill of his Companions and said that if anyone gave charity equal to Mount Uhud in gold, it would still not reach even one Mudd of a Companion's charity.

mcqs.q: What rank do the Companions (RA) hold among human beings?
options: They are equal in rank to the angels
They rank below the later scholars
They rank only above their own generation
After the Prophets (AS), they hold the highest glory and rank among all human beings on earth
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that after the Prophets they hold the highest rank. Keeping heartfelt love and devotion for this pure group is exactly faith, whereas showing even a little disrespect in their honour is a great sin.

mcqs.q: What does 'Ashra Mubashra' mean?
options: The ten Companions to whom the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave the glad tidings of Paradise in this world itself
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise in this world. 'Ashrah' means ten and 'Mubashsharah' comes from 'Basharah', glad tidings; their names are recorded in Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith 3747.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Companions is among the Ashra Mubashra?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Talhah (RA). The Ashra Mubashra are Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Talhah, Zubayr, Abdur Rahman bin Awf, Sa'd, Sa'eed and Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (may Allah be pleased with them all), as listed in Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith 3747.

mcqs.q: In the hadith of glad tidings ('Tooba liman ra'ani...'), to whom are glad tidings given?
options: Only to the people of Madinah
To the one who saw the Prophet (PBUH) and believed, and also to the one who saw such a person who had seen him
Only to those present at Badr
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to the one who saw him and believed, and to the one who saw that person. In this hadith, glad tidings have been given to the Companion (Sahabi) and to the Tabi'i, the one who saw a Companion (Mizan-ul-I'tidal by Adh-Dhahabi).

mcqs.q: What lesson should we take from the Companions (RA) for our daily life?
options: Visit the cities where they lived
Adopt their truthfulness, trustworthiness, sacrifice and obedience to the Messenger (PBUH) in our own life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to adopt their qualities in our own life. We should take lessons from the truthfulness, trustworthiness, sacrifice, patience, justice and service to creation of the Companions and the Ashra Mubashra, and keep their love and respect in our hearts.

chapters.title: Akhlaq — Ilm, Khandan, Respect for Humanity, Adl and Haya

lessons.title: Importance and Virtue of Knowledge
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Ilm

  • The literal meaning of Ilm is knowing and becoming aware.
  • The word Taleem is used for giving and teaching knowledge to others.
  • In technical terms, knowing the reality of a thing through man's five senses and intellect is called Ilm.

Why Knowledge Makes Man Honourable

  • The Lord of the universe made man the noblest of creation (Ashraf-ul-Makhlooqat) and blessed him with knowledge and intellect.
  • Through knowledge alone, the whole universe was made subservient for man.
  • Knowledge alone is the cause of man attaining honour over all other creation.
  • Knowledge alone is the basis of greatness and honour for man, and the means of exaltation.
  • It is an attribute of Allah Almighty: He holds the attributes of Knower of the Unseen and Knower of what is in the hearts; that Being alone grants to all creation the knowledge of its need.

Islam and the Value of Knowledge

  • At the time when Islam began in Arabia, the world was unaware of the importance of knowledge.
  • Islam revealed the value and worth of knowledge, and created in people the desire to acquire knowledge.
  • Surah Al-Mujadilah (11): Those among you who believed, and those who were given knowledge — Allah Almighty will raise their ranks. Here, in high ranks, knowledge has been mentioned along with faith.
  • Surah Taha (114): O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge.

Hadith on Knowledge and Scholars

Hadith — the scholars are the heirs of the Prophets: إِنَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَرَثَةُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ

  • Translation: The scholars alone are the heirs of the Prophets (AS). (Sunan Tirmidhi, Hadith: 2682)
  • One understanding scholar is heavier for Satan than a thousand worshippers. (Sunan Ibn Majah: 222)

Hadith — seeking knowledge is obligatory: طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ

  • Translation: Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim (man and woman). (Sunan Ibn Majah: 224)

The Holy Prophet ﷺ as a Teacher

  • He ﷺ taught with gentleness and ease.
  • He ﷺ explained with examples.
  • He ﷺ took care of the mental level of the students.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Ilm'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is knowing and becoming aware. The word 'Taleem' is used for giving and teaching knowledge to others, while Ilm in technical terms means knowing the reality of a thing through man's five senses and intellect.

mcqs.q: In technical terms, what is Ilm (knowledge)?
options: Knowing the reality of a thing through man's five senses and intellect
Listening to stories of the past
mcqs.why: The correct answer is knowing the reality of a thing through the five senses and intellect. This real knowledge is what made man the noblest of creation and the basis of his greatness and honour among all creatures.

mcqs.q: Because of knowledge, what honour was given to man by Allah Almighty?
options: He was given control over the angels
He was made the noblest of creation (Ashraf-ul-Makhlooqat) and the whole universe was made subservient for him
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that man was made Ashraf-ul-Makhlooqat, the noblest of creation. Allah blessed man with knowledge and intellect, and through knowledge alone the whole universe was made subservient for him, making knowledge the means of his exaltation.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Mujadilah, verse 11, what will Allah Almighty do for those who believed and those who were given knowledge?
options: He will excuse them from Salah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that He will raise their ranks. In Surah Al-Mujadilah, verse 11, knowledge is mentioned along with faith in connection with high ranks, showing the exalted position of knowledge in Islam.

mcqs.q: Which dua for knowledge is taught in Surah Taha, verse 114?
options: 'O my Sustainer! Increase me in wealth'
'O my Sustainer! Increase me in strength'
'O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge'
'O my Sustainer! Increase me in children'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'O my Sustainer! Increase me in knowledge.' This dua of Surah Taha, verse 114 teaches a believer to keep asking Allah for more knowledge, because Islam revealed the value of knowledge at a time when the world was unaware of its importance.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sunan Tirmidhi (2682), the scholars are what in relation to the Prophets (AS)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the heirs of the Prophets. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'Indeed, the scholars are the heirs of the Prophets,' which gives scholars an honoured station as carriers of the Prophets' legacy of knowledge.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Ibn Majah (222), one understanding scholar is heavier for Satan than how many worshippers?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a thousand worshippers. The hadith states that one understanding scholar (a faqih with insight) is heavier upon Satan than a thousand worshippers, because knowledge protects a person and others from Satan's deception.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Ibn Majah (224), seeking knowledge is what upon every Muslim?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is obligatory upon every Muslim. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'Seeking knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim,' so acquiring the necessary knowledge is a duty, not a choice, for every Muslim man and woman.

mcqs.q: How did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) teach as a teacher?
options: With strictness and long lectures only
With gentleness and ease, explaining with examples and taking care of the mental level of the students
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with gentleness, examples and care for the students' mental level. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) taught with gentleness and ease, explained matters with examples, and always kept in view the mental level of those he taught.

mcqs.q: Knowledge is an attribute of Allah Almighty in which sense, as stated in the lesson?
options: He is the Knower of the Unseen and the Knower of what is in the hearts, and He grants every creature the knowledge of its need
He shares all His knowledge with every person equally
He needs knowledge from His creation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah is the Knower of the Unseen and of what is in the hearts. Knowledge is His attribute, and that Being alone grants to all creation the knowledge of its need, which is why seeking knowledge draws a person nearer to his Creator.

lessons.title: Importance of Family in Islam
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Family?

  • Khandan (family) is a Persian word, whose literal meaning is household, family, tribe, children and lineage.
  • The collection of close relatives of the same generation is the concept of family life.
  • The important members of the family — mother, father, wife, husband and children — hold basic status.
  • Social life begins with the family and household. The family begins with the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman (husband and wife).
  • Apart from man, the concept of family and relations does not exist in any other creation. This honour belongs to man, the noblest of creation, that he behaves at home with respect and honour, love and affection, in the capacity of mother, father, grandparents, siblings and children.

Family in Islam

  • On this principle, Islam gives equal importance to man and woman. Each one's sphere is fixed.
  • Islam exhorts and emphasises the fulfilment of the rights and duties of each one.
  • Surah Al-Hujurat (13): O mankind! Indeed, We created you from one man and one woman.
  • The relationship of husband and wife: the survival of humanity and the existence of the human race is through the joint relationship of man and woman. This relationship holds great importance.
  • The objectives of family and married life: in the sight of Allah Almighty, the objective of family life is the survival of the human race and its increase.
  • Man gets peace and contentment only through married life. The mutual love and affection of husband and wife becomes the means of comfort and peace of family life.
  • Through Nikah, the chain of the human race continues with survival, and with human greatness and honour.

Rights and Duties of Husband and Wife

  • According to Islamic teachings, some rights and duties of the spouses upon each other have been fixed.

Verse — equal rights of spouses (Al-Baqarah: 228): وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوْفِ

  • Translation: And the rights of women upon men are the same as, according to custom, the rights of men upon women.
  • Providing food and drink, expenses, clothing, house, treatment and other needs is the responsibility of the husband, which he will fulfil according to his financial means.
  • Apart from giving the wife the permission to keep mahr, given money or other personal property, and to do business within permissible limits, it is also among the duties of the husband that he behaves with love and affection with the wife and other members of the house, does not oppress or wrong them, adopts the behaviour of justice and kindness, and fulfils their rights according to Shariah.
  • The responsibility of the wife is that in the absence of the husband, she protects wealth and property and her honour like a trust, and does not give permission to any non-mahram to enter the house without the permission of the husband.

Verse — the righteous women (An-Nisa: 34): فَالصَّالِحَاتُ قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهُ

  • Translation: So the righteous women are obedient, and protect their wealth and honour in their absence.
  • She should not demand expenses more than the income and financial status of the husband. If she sees hardship or straitness in the husband's house, she should not complain about it to others unnecessarily; rather she should show overlooking and endurance.
  • She should not reveal the secrets of the husband or the house. She should protect the lineage, and take better care and training of the children. She should serve and obey the husband.

Hadith — the best for his family: خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ وَأَنَا خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِي

  • Translation: The best among you is the one who is best for his family, and I am the best among you for my family. (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 2052)

Respect for Parents

  • Among all relations, the relation of parents is important and worthy of respect. It is because of them that we came into this world, and with their care and upbringing, strength developed in us. Therefore, we should not be negligent in serving and respecting parents.
  • Surah Al-Isra (23-24): Your Sustainer has commanded that you worship none besides Him (Allah), and do good to parents. If one of them or both of them reach old age before you, and become angry over some matter, beware! Do not even say "Uff" to them in reply, and do not scold them, and speak with great respect. And lower your neck in humility with kindness before them, and say: O my Sustainer! Have mercy on them, as they raised me with mercy when I was small.
  • The rights of parents upon children are: honour and respect, obedience and submission, good conduct, good conduct with the near ones and companions of parents, confession of gratitude, and dua for forgiveness.

Rights of Children

  • Giving children the training of the necessary matters of the religion, the education of the Holy Quran, and Salah.
  • Teaching children Islamic values, dealing with equality and justice among children in inheritance.
  • Including daughters also, like sons, in gifts and love. Not becoming sad at the birth of a daughter, because expressing displeasure is ingratitude.
  • Avoiding every kind of harshness and violence against children. Keeping a behaviour of kindness and love and affection with them.
  • Not killing one's children because of hunger and poverty.
  • The charm of the family is children, and having children is a great blessing of Allah Almighty.
  • Those relatives with whom Nikah cannot take place are called Mahram.

Acts That Harm the Family

  • Misuse of mobile and internet, disobedience to parents, household quarrels, distrust in relations, wasteful spending, giving preference to outside friends over home.

mcqs.q: The word 'Khandan' (family) belongs to which language, and what does it mean?
options: It is a Persian word meaning household, family, tribe, children and lineage
It is an Arabic word meaning neighbours
It is a Turkish word meaning army
It is a Sindhi word meaning village
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Khandan is a Persian word meaning household, family, tribe, children and lineage. The important members of the family, mother, father, husband, wife and children, hold basic status, and social life begins with the family.

mcqs.q: With what does the family begin in Islam?
options: With the birth of the first child
With the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman (husband and wife)
With the earning of the husband
mcqs.why: The correct answer is with the mutual Nikah of a man and a woman. Through Nikah the chain of the human race continues, man finds peace and contentment in married life, and apart from man, the concept of family and relations does not exist in any other creation.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 228, what is the relation between the rights of wives and husbands?
options: Women have no rights upon men
The rights of women upon men are the same as the rights of men upon women, according to custom
Men have double the rights in every matter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that their rights are equal according to custom. The verse 'Walahunna mithlul-lazi alaihinna bil-ma'roof' (Al-Baqarah, 228) establishes mutual rights and duties of the spouses upon each other in Islamic teachings.

mcqs.q: Which responsibilities towards the wife rest upon the husband?
options: Keeping her away from all relatives
Providing food and drink, expenses, clothing, house and treatment according to his financial means
mcqs.why: The correct answer is providing all her needs according to his means. It is also the husband's duty to behave with love and affection, not to oppress her, and to adopt justice and kindness towards the wife and other members of the house.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nisa, verse 34, who are the righteous women?
options: Those who earn more than their husbands
Those who are obedient and protect (their husband's wealth and their own honour) in his absence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is those who are obedient and protect in the husband's absence. The verse describes righteous women as 'Qanitat' (obedient) and 'Hafizat lil-ghaib' (guardians in absence), protecting wealth and honour like a trust.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Sunan Ibn Majah (2052), who is the best among you?
options: The one who is best for his family
The one who is most famous
The one who travels the most
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who is best for his family. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'The best among you is the one who is best for his family, and I am the best among you for my family' (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 2052).

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Isra, verses 23-24, what must a person NOT do when his parents reach old age?
options: He must not live with them
He must not even say 'Uff' to them, nor scold them
He must not ask their advice
He must not spend on them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he must not even say 'Uff' to them, nor scold them. Instead, he should speak to them with great respect, lower his neck in humility with kindness before them, and pray: 'O my Sustainer! Have mercy on them, as they raised me with mercy when I was small.'

mcqs.q: Which of the following is included among the rights of parents upon their children?
options: Good conduct with the near ones and companions of the parents, and dua for their forgiveness
mcqs.why: The correct answer includes good conduct with the parents' near ones and companions, and dua for their forgiveness. The rights of parents are: honour and respect, obedience and submission, good conduct, confession of gratitude, and prayer for their forgiveness.

mcqs.q: Who are 'Mahram' relatives?
options: Those relatives with whom Nikah cannot take place
Those relatives who are older in age
mcqs.why: The correct answer is those relatives with whom Nikah cannot take place. Such relations are called Mahram, and the rules of family life, including who may enter the house, are connected with this category of relatives.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a right of children upon their parents?
options: Dealing with equality and justice among children, and including daughters, like sons, in gifts and love
Giving sons everything and daughters nothing
Becoming sad at the birth of a daughter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dealing with equality and justice among children, including daughters in gifts and love. Parents must also give children religious training and Quran education, avoid harshness and violence against them, and not be displeased at a daughter's birth, for that is ingratitude.

lessons.title: Respect for Humanity
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Respect for Humanity

  • Ihtiram means honour and value, virtue and superiority.
  • Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat means the honour and greatness of man.
  • Man is the best creation of Allah Almighty on earth; he has superiority over all creation.
  • Every human being has the rank and status of honour and virtue; protecting the life, wealth and honour of every human being — whatever his colour, race, religion, language, nation and country — on behalf of his humanity is called "Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat".

The Quran on Human Honour

  • The Holy Quran has stated great honour for man, and Allah Almighty has granted man great honour and dignity (Surah Al-Isra: 70).

Verse — honour of the children of Adam (Surah Al-Isra: 70): وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنَا بَنِيْ آدَمَ

  • Translation: We have granted honour to the children of Adam.

Verse — the most honourable is the most pious (Al-Hujurat: 13): إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ

  • Translation: Indeed, the most honourable among you in the sight of Allah Almighty is the one who is most pious.
  • Islam declared the distinction of colour, race, language and homeland invalid, and the standard of greatness and nobility is only Taqwa and the fear of Allah Almighty (Al-Hujurat: 13).
  • The Holy Quran informed man of his correct station: Allah Almighty made him the caliph and deputy on earth, and informed him of everything, and freed him from the slavery of all his objects of worship.
  • In all these blessed verses, generally, only man has been given status, whether Muslim or non-Muslim.

Before Islam and the Teaching of Islam

  • The era before Islam is called the "Age of Ignorance", in which respect for humanity had almost ended.
  • Islam, rejecting false ideas and customs, taught human beings the lesson of respect for humanity, and declared qualities like arrogance and self-liking as bad.
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: O mankind! You are all the children of one father; therefore, any person considering himself greater than others and being arrogant is a matter of foolishness and ignorance (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 23489).

Acts Against Respect for Humanity

  • Being arrogant, considering oneself worthy of pride before Allah Almighty or creation, in intellectual, scholarly, financial or lineage terms.
  • Considering people inferior, adopting a mocking or joking behaviour with them, and making accusations.
  • Showing oppression, excess or injustice with people, finding faults in them, trying to spy.
  • Taunting a person because of his physical or practical shortcoming, calling him by bad nicknames, or dishonouring him in any way.
  • Treating children unequally on the basis of young and old, wise and unwise, or son and daughter.
  • Talking to one another with immorality, foul language or in a bad manner. Examples of respect in daily life are helping a poor person and respecting elders.

mcqs.q: What is meant by Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat (respect for humanity)?
options: Protecting the life, wealth and honour of every human being, whatever his colour, race, religion, language, nation and country
Respecting only the rich and powerful
Respecting only people of one's own religion
mcqs.why: The correct answer is protecting the life, wealth and honour of every human being without distinction. Every human being has the rank of honour, so this protection is owed to him on behalf of his humanity, whatever his colour, race, religion, language, nation or country may be.

mcqs.q: Which verse of Surah Al-Isra (verse 70) declares the honour of mankind?
options: 'We created man in the best form'
'We made you into nations and tribes'
'We have granted honour to the children of Adam'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'We have granted honour to the children of Adam' (Surah Al-Isra, 70). The Holy Quran has stated great honour for man, and Allah Almighty made him His caliph and deputy on earth.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Hujurat, verse 13, what is the only standard of honour and nobility in the sight of Allah?
options: Taqwa, the fear of Allah and piety
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Taqwa. The verse declares: 'Indeed, the most honourable among you in the sight of Allah is the one who is most pious,' and Islam declared the distinctions of colour, race, language and homeland invalid.

mcqs.q: To whom does the honour granted by the Quran apply?
options: To all human beings generally, whether Muslim or non-Muslim
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to all human beings, Muslim or non-Muslim. In the blessed verses about human honour, generally only man as such has been given this status, and Islam taught this lesson after an age in which respect for humanity had almost ended.

mcqs.q: What is the era before Islam called, in which respect for humanity had almost ended?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Age of Ignorance. Islam, rejecting the false ideas and customs of that age, taught human beings the lesson of respect for humanity and declared qualities like arrogance and self-liking to be bad.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Musnad Ahmad (23489), considering oneself greater than others and being arrogant is what?
options: A matter of foolishness and ignorance, because all people are the children of one father
mcqs.why: The correct answer is foolishness and ignorance. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'O mankind! You are all the children of one father,' so no person has any basis for considering himself greater than others and being arrogant.

mcqs.q: Which of the following acts is against respect for humanity?
options: Taunting a person because of a physical or practical shortcoming and calling him by bad nicknames
mcqs.why: The correct answer is taunting a person for a shortcoming and calling him by bad nicknames. Mocking people, considering them inferior, spying on them, finding their faults and dishonouring them in any way are all against Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat.

mcqs.q: Treating children unequally on the basis of being a son or a daughter is counted as what?
options: An act against respect for humanity
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an act against respect for humanity. Treating children unequally on the basis of young and old, wise and unwise, or son and daughter violates the honour due to every human being, just like oppression, foul language and arrogance do.

mcqs.q: Which examples of respect for humanity in daily life are given in the lesson?
options: Helping a poor person and respecting elders
mcqs.why: The correct answer is helping a poor person and respecting elders. These simple daily acts put Ihtiram-e-Insaniyat into practice, opposite to arrogance, mockery, oppression and fault-finding, which destroy it.

mcqs.q: What station did Allah Almighty inform man of, along with his honour?
options: He made man a servant of other men
He made man dependent on kings
He made man a worshipper of nature
He made man His caliph and deputy on earth and freed him from the slavery of all his (false) objects of worship
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Allah made man His caliph and deputy on earth. The Quran informed man of his correct station: he is Allah's deputy on earth, freed from the slavery of all his objects of worship, and honoured above all creation.

lessons.title: Social Justice
lessons.notes_html:
Meaning of Adl

  • Adl is an Arabic word, whose literal meaning is: to straighten, to equalise, to compare between two things, and to adopt moderation between two conditions.
  • In technical terms, the concept of Adl is very vast: placing a thing in its correct place, that is, fully abiding by truth in word and deed, dealing with every person without any favour or concession, giving him what he deserves, is "Adl".
  • Against Adl comes Zulm (oppression), that is, placing a thing out of place.
  • "Adl" with an oppressor is that he should be prevented from oppressing.

Quranic Guidance on Collective Justice

  • Surah An-Nahl (90): Indeed, Allah Almighty commands justice, goodness, and giving to relatives, and forbids immodesty, evil talk and oppression. He advises you so that you may understand.
  • The purpose of the revelation of this verse is that all human beings should live with justice and fairness in their collective life, and end oppression and excess, so that their social life becomes a centre of peace and tranquillity.
  • Surah An-Nisa (58): When you judge between people, judge with justice. Indeed, Allah Almighty advises you a very good thing. Surely Allah Almighty is All-Hearing.
  • The meaning of "when you judge between people" is that for the one who judges, both parties should be equal, whether he is a friend or an enemy, one's own or a stranger, Muslim or non-Muslim, near or far, rich or poor.

Verse — justice is closer to Taqwa (Al-Ma'idah: 8): اِعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ

  • Translation: Do justice, because it is closer to Taqwa.
  • If justice and fairness are established in the country, society will become peaceful and tranquil. Islam is the religion of peace and security, and with justice, social life becomes a centre of peace and tranquillity.

Evils of Ignoring Collective Justice

  • By ignoring justice, restlessness and corruption are created in society; the first cause of corruption is deviating from "Adl" (justice).
  • Corruption is created in society when its members abandon "Adl".
  • By not establishing justice in the economy, society does not become prosperous, and some member of society remains deprived of basic needs.
  • Without establishing equality in all spheres of life, man's life cannot become better, because special balance and moderation in all spheres of life is necessary.

Measures to Establish Collective Justice

  • Legal equality — there should be legal equality in society, that is, all are equal in the eyes of the law, and the law should apply to all without exception (whether rich or poor, officer or subordinate, friend or enemy).
  • Collective justice in economic matters — every person should be free to adopt a lawful means of livelihood according to his abilities and choice, and lawful means of earning a livelihood should not be closed for any person.
  • Collective justice in judicial matters — Islam has presented a regular system of justice, which is called "Qaza" or "judiciary".
  • Establishment of a just society — all human beings are equal as human beings; no one has superiority because of belonging to a class, family, nation or region.

mcqs.q: What are the literal meanings of the word 'Adl'?
options: To punish, to imprison and to fine
To gather, to store and to distribute
To straighten, to equalise, to compare between two things and to adopt moderation between two conditions
To command, to forbid and to warn
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to straighten, equalise, compare and adopt moderation. In technical terms, Adl means placing a thing in its correct place, abiding by truth in word and deed, and giving every person what he deserves without favour or concession.

mcqs.q: In technical terms, what is Adl (justice)?
options: Giving everyone exactly the same wealth
Placing a thing in its correct place and giving every person what he deserves without any favour
Always favouring the poor against the rich
mcqs.why: The correct answer is placing a thing in its correct place and giving each his due without favour. Its opposite is Zulm (oppression), which means placing a thing out of place, and Adl with an oppressor means preventing him from oppressing.

mcqs.q: What is Zulm, the opposite of Adl?
options: Placing a thing out of its place
Placing a thing in its correct place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is placing a thing out of its place. Adl is putting everything where it belongs and dealing with every person according to truth, while Zulm is the displacement of things from their rightful position, which breeds corruption in society.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nahl, verse 90, what does Allah Almighty command and what does He forbid?
options: He commands trade and travel, and forbids farming
He commands silence, and forbids questions
He commands migration, and forbids settling
He commands justice, goodness (Ihsan) and giving to relatives, and forbids immodesty, evil talk and oppression
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that He commands justice, Ihsan and giving to relatives, and forbids immodesty, evil and oppression. The purpose of this verse is that all human beings should live with justice and fairness in their collective life, so society becomes a centre of peace and tranquillity.

mcqs.q: According to Surah An-Nisa, verse 58, how should the one who judges between people treat the two parties?
options: He should favour his friends and relatives
He should favour the rich party
Both parties should be equal for him, whether friend or enemy, one's own or a stranger, Muslim or non-Muslim, rich or poor
He should favour the party of his own religion only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that both parties should be equal for the judge. The verse commands: 'When you judge between people, judge with justice,' without any distinction of friend or enemy, near or far, rich or poor.

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Ma'idah, verse 8, justice is closer to what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Taqwa. Allah commands: 'Do justice, because it is closer to Taqwa,' and when justice and fairness are established in a country, society becomes peaceful and tranquil, for Islam is the religion of peace and security.

mcqs.q: What is stated to be the first cause of corruption in society?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is deviating from Adl. By ignoring justice, restlessness and corruption are created in society; corruption appears when its members abandon justice, and without economic justice some members remain deprived of basic needs.

mcqs.q: What does legal equality, a measure for establishing collective justice, require?
options: Different laws for the rich and the poor
Exemption of officers from the law
All are equal in the eyes of the law, and the law applies to all without exception, rich or poor, officer or subordinate
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that all are equal before the law without exception. Legal equality is one of the measures to establish collective justice, together with economic justice, a proper judiciary and the equality of all human beings as human beings.

mcqs.q: What does collective justice in economic matters require?
options: The state should fix one occupation for everyone
Only the rich may do business
Every person should be free to adopt a lawful means of livelihood according to his abilities and choice, and lawful earning must not be closed for anyone
Trade should be banned for some classes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is freedom to adopt any lawful livelihood. Without establishing justice in the economy, society does not become prosperous, and without equality and balance in all spheres of life, man's life cannot become better.

mcqs.q: What is the regular system of justice presented by Islam called?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qaza, the judiciary. Islam has presented a regular system for justice in judicial matters called Qaza, and in a just society no one has superiority because of class, family, nation or region.

lessons.title: Iffat and Haya (Chastity and Modesty)
lessons.notes_html:
Concepts of Iffat, Ismat and Haya
