  • Iffat is an Arabic word, whose literal meaning is piety and purity, and the Shariah concept of Iffat is: remaining chaste, adopting moral purity, and keeping the desires of the self under control, and protecting the self from walking on a bad path, and from acts like adultery and immodesty.
  • Along with it comes another word, Ismat, whose meaning is chastity, innocence and nobility.
  • The literal meaning of Haya is shame and self-respect (Ghairat). The meaning of Haya is: a natural and moral quality has been placed inside man, by which man, due to the feeling of the fear of God, saves himself from bad acts like immodesty and immorality, and tries to stay away from evil; such a person is called modest (Haya-dar).

Importance of Iffat and Haya

  • Iffat and Haya holds the status of soul and life in the list of Islamic morals.
  • Allah Almighty taught the Muslims Iffat and Haya, and gave this great quality the highest place among all Islamic virtues.
  • Iffat and Haya are the basis of man's nobility, honour and chastity.
  • When man destroys his Haya, then he becomes like a wild beast, and runs after his desires.

Virtue in the Quran and Hadith

Verse — those who guard their chastity (Al-Mu'minoon: 5): وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ

  • Translation: And (the successful believer is) the one who protects his private parts.
  • Every religion has some morals, and the morals of Islam is Haya. (Muwatta Imam Malik, Hadith: 2634)
  • Indeed, Allah Almighty is Modest and Concealing, and He likes modesty and concealment. (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4012)

Hadith — Haya is a branch of faith: وَالْحَيَاءُ شُعْبَةٌ مِنَ الْإِيمَانِ

  • Translation: And Haya is a great branch of faith. (Bukhari: 9, Muslim: 30)
  • It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Faith has more than seventy branches, among which Haya is also a great branch. (Bukhari: 9, Muslim: 30)
  • It is narrated from Hazrat Umar (RA): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Indeed, faith and Haya have a deep connection with each other. When one goes, the other also goes. (Al-Adab-ul-Mufrad by Al-Bukhari: 1313)
  • Some wise men have stated the ranks of Haya to be three: 1. Following the commands of God and avoiding forbidden things, 2. Staying away from harming people, 3. Being modest with oneself in solitude, and considering Allah present in every condition and avoiding sins.

The Haya of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) that: Our beloved Prophet, the Holy Prophet ﷺ, was the most Iffat- and Haya-possessing of all.
  • He ﷺ was more modest than even a virgin veiled woman, and if he saw something disliked, its effect used to appear on his blessed face. Whereas he ﷺ had a natural hatred for other (evil) things. (Sunan Abi Dawood, Hadith: 4797)

Manifestations of Iffat and Haya

  • Man's Iffat and Haya is not only related to his character and action, but it also has great importance in his thought and thinking, speech and manner. Every Muslim man and woman should give priority to Iffat and Haya in his way of life, so that he is counted as a respectable, useful citizen of society, and a person preparing for the Hereafter.
  • Conversation — It is not appropriate for a believer to talk with abuse, foul language and in an unpleasant manner; rather he should adopt good talk or silence.
  • Dress — Islam has stated two purposes of dress: one, that it should have covering (Satr), and second, that it should also have adornment (Zeenat). Therefore, men and women should, keeping in view their Haya and veil, adopt such dress in which both these purposes are attained.
  • Sitting and rising — A true believer should avoid immodesty and indecent activities at all times in his daily routines. The Holy Quran commands believing men and women that they should keep their gazes lowered and protect their Iffat and Ismat.
  • Gathering — A person spends some hours in some gathering, meeting or consultative activity; therefore, whatever time is spent among people, during that time too, Iffat and Haya should remain in his sitting, rising, conversation and manner.

mcqs.q: What is the Shariah concept of Iffat?
options: Remaining chaste, adopting moral purity, keeping the desires of the self under control and protecting oneself from bad paths like adultery and immodesty
mcqs.why: The correct answer is remaining chaste and keeping the desires of the self under control. Iffat literally means piety and purity, and together with Haya it holds the status of soul and life in the list of Islamic morals.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'Ismat' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is chastity, innocence and nobility. Ismat comes along with Iffat in this lesson, and the Holy Quran commands believing men and women to keep their gazes lowered and to protect their Iffat and Ismat.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of Haya?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is shame and self-respect (Ghairat). Haya is a natural and moral quality placed inside man, by which, due to the feeling of the fear of God, he saves himself from immodesty and immorality, and such a person is called Haya-dar (modest).

mcqs.q: According to Surah Al-Mu'minoon, verse 5, who is the successful believer?
options: The one who owns much property
The one who guards and protects his private parts (his chastity)
The one who has many children
The one who travels for trade
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the one who guards his chastity. The verse says: 'And (the successful believers are) those who protect their private parts,' placing the guarding of chastity among the qualities of the successful believers.

mcqs.q: Complete the hadith recorded in Muwatta Imam Malik (2634): 'Every religion has some morals, and the morals of Islam is ____.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Haya. This hadith shows the central place of modesty in Islam: Allah taught the Muslims Iffat and Haya and gave this quality the highest place among all Islamic virtues, as the basis of man's nobility, honour and chastity.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Abi Dawood (4012), what does Allah Almighty like?
options: Modesty and concealment, for He is Modest and Concealing
mcqs.why: The correct answer is modesty and concealment. The hadith states: 'Indeed, Allah Almighty is Modest and Concealing, and He likes modesty and concealment,' teaching believers to value Haya in their own conduct.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith narrated by Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) (Bukhari 9, Muslim 30), how many branches does faith have, and what is Haya among them?
options: Faith has more than seventy branches, and Haya is a great branch of faith
Faith has five branches, and Haya is the last of them
Faith has forty branches, and Haya is not among them
Faith has ten branches, and Haya is the first of them
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that faith has more than seventy branches and Haya is a great branch of it. The hadith 'Al-Haya'u shu'batun min al-Iman' (Haya is a branch of faith) is recorded in Sahih Bukhari, Hadith 9, and Sahih Muslim, Hadith 30.

mcqs.q: According to the narration of Hazrat Umar (RA) in Al-Adab-ul-Mufrad (1313), what is the connection between faith and Haya?
options: They have a deep connection with each other; when one goes, the other also goes
Haya comes only after faith is complete
Faith remains even when Haya is destroyed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that when one goes, the other also goes. Faith and Haya are deeply connected, and when a man destroys his Haya he becomes like a wild beast running after his desires.

mcqs.q: How modest was the Holy Prophet (PBUH), according to Hazrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA)?
options: He was less modest than ordinary people
His modesty appeared only in the mosque
He never showed any dislike on his face
He was more modest than even a virgin veiled woman, and dislike of anything showed on his blessed face
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he was more modest than a veiled virgin. Hazrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) narrated that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) possessed the most Iffat and Haya of all, and if he saw something he disliked, its effect appeared on his blessed face (Sunan Abi Dawood, 4797).

mcqs.q: According to Islam, what are the two purposes of dress?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is covering (Satr) and adornment (Zeenat). Men and women should adopt such dress, keeping Haya and veil in view, in which both purposes are attained, just as a believer should adopt good talk or silence and avoid immodest activities in gatherings.

chapters.title: Mashahir-e-Islam — Imam Hussain, Abu Ubaidah, Jabir bin Hayyan and Muhammad Rashid Rozay Dhani

lessons.title: Hazrat Syedna Imam Hussain (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Lineage and Family

  • His full name is Husain bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib bin Hashim.
  • His father is Sher-e-Khuda Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).
  • His mother is Khatoon-e-Jannat Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra (RA), the daughter of Hazrat Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
  • From both the mother's and father's sides, he is Hashmi, a possessor of honour and virtue.

Virtues in the Ahadith of the Holy Prophet ﷺ

  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: "Fatimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, and Hasan and Husain are the leaders of the youth of Paradise." (Sunan Tirmidhi: 3781)
  • Loving Hazrat Hasan and Husain (RA) is equal to loving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and hating both of them is equal to hating the Holy Prophet ﷺ.

Hadith on loving Hasan and Husain: مَنْ أَحَبَّ الْحَسَنَ وَالْحُسَيْنَ فَقَدْ أَحَبَّنِي، وَمَنْ أَبْغَضَهُمَا فَقَدْ أَبْغَضَنِي

  • Translation: Whoever loves Hasan and Husain, indeed he loves me; and whoever hates them, indeed he hates me.

Hadith — Husain is from me: حُسَيْنٌ مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْ حُسَيْنٍ، أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ أَحَبَّ حُسَيْنًا، حُسَيْنٌ سِبْطٌ مِنَ الْأَسْبَاطِ

  • Translation: Husain is from me, and I am from Husain. May Allah Almighty love the one who loved Husain. Husain is a grandson among grandsons. (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 144)
  • Once, the Holy Prophet ﷺ was going with the Companions to an invitation, when in a street of Madinah Munawwarah he saw Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) playing with children; he caught him smiling, kissed his forehead, and said this hadith.

Hadith on awe, leadership, courage and generosity: أَمَّا الْحَسَنُ، فَلَهُ هَيْبَتِي وَسُؤْدُدِي وَأَمَّا الْحُسَيْنُ، فَلَهُ جَرَاءَتِي وَجُودِي

  • Translation: I granted my awe and leadership to Hasan, and I granted my courage and generosity to Husain. (Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabeer by At-Tabarani: 18508)

Character — Correcting a Person's Wudu

  • Sayyiduna Imam Husain (RA) was, from childhood, a possessor of high Seerah and morals in intelligence and wisdom.
  • Once, he went to the mosque with his brother Sayyiduna Imam Hasan (RA), and saw that a person was doing Wudu, but his method of doing Wudu was not correct.
  • He said to him: "O uncle! We both are doing Wudu; see whether we are making any mistake in Wudu."
  • When both Imams did Wudu, that person was astonished to see that they were doing Wudu correctly, but his Wudu was not correct.
  • In this way, he corrected his Wudu without embarrassing that person. (Bihar-ul-Anwar, Imam Majlisi 43, p. 319)

Refusal of Yazid's Bay'at and the Tragedy of Karbala

  • After Yazid sat on the throne, on the order of the governor of Madinah Munawwarah, Sayyiduna Imam Husain (RA) was called to pledge Bay'at to Yazid, but he refused to pledge Bay'at and set out for Makkah Mukarramah.
  • He stayed in Makkah Mukarramah for four months.
  • During that time, the people of Kufa sent letters to him that he should come to Kufa, so that they may pledge Bay'at at his hand, because besides him, they have no leader and Imam, and in the Yazidi government, Islamic traditions are being trampled.
  • After that, Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) sent his cousin Muslim bin Aqeel (RA) to Kufa, so that he may go and assess the conditions there.
  • Meanwhile, Yazid was informed of the coming of Muslim bin Aqeel, so Yazid removed the governor of Kufa, Hazrat Nu'man bin Bashir (RA), and appointed Ubaidullah bin Ziyad as governor, and ordered him that the representative of Imam Husain (RA), Muslim bin Aqeel (RA), should be imprisoned or killed.
  • Meanwhile, Muslim bin Aqeel had already informed Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) that he should come to Kufa; the people of Kufa have pledged Bay'at to him — but on the other side, Ibn Ziyad had Muslim bin Aqeel martyred.
  • Imam Husain (RA), along with his family, set out from Makkah Mukarramah for Kufa on 8 Dhu-ul-Hijjah 60 Hijri, and after a very difficult journey of forty-four days, reached the plain of Karbala on 2 Muharram-ul-Haram 61 Hijri.
  • The commander of the Yazidi army, Umar bin Sa'd, insisted that Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) pledge Bay'at to Yazid; this series continued from 2 Muharram-ul-Haram to 10 Muharram-ul-Haram, but Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) clearly refused to pledge Bay'at to Yazid and to bow before falsehood.
  • Finally, on 10 Muharram-ul-Haram 61 Hijri, the battle of truth and falsehood took place, in which Hazrat Imam Husain (RA), along with his family and devoted ones, was martyred one by one.
  • Today, the city of Karbala is a famous city of Iraq, where the blessed shrine of Sayyiduna Imam Husain (RA) is located, and that is his resting place.

mcqs.q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Imam Husain (RA)?
options: Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra (RA), the daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hazrat Fatimah-uz-Zahra (RA). Imam Husain's full name is Husain bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib bin Hashim; his father is Sher-e-Khuda Hazrat Ali (RA), and from both sides he is Hashmi.

mcqs.q: According to Sunan Tirmidhi (3781), Hazrat Hasan and Hazrat Husain (RA) are the leaders of whom?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the youth of Paradise. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: 'Fatimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, and Hasan and Husain are the leaders of the youth of Paradise' (Sunan Tirmidhi, 3781).

mcqs.q: Complete the hadith in Sunan Ibn Majah (144): 'Husain is from me, and I am from ____.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Husain: 'Husain is from me, and I am from Husain. May Allah love the one who loved Husain. Husain is a grandson (Sibt) among the grandsons' (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith 144). The Prophet (PBUH) spoke these words after kissing the young Husain's forehead in a street of Madinah.

mcqs.q: According to the hadith in Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabeer by At-Tabarani (18508), what did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) grant to Hazrat Husain (RA)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his courage and generosity. The Prophet (PBUH) said: 'As for Hasan, I granted him my awe and leadership; and as for Husain, I granted him my courage and generosity' (Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabeer, 18508).

mcqs.q: How did the young Imam Husain (RA) correct the Wudu of a man in the mosque, along with Imam Hasan (RA)?
options: Both brothers performed Wudu before him and asked him to check their mistakes, so the man realised his own error without being embarrassed
They openly scolded him in the mosque
They complained about him to the people
They asked him to leave the mosque
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they performed Wudu before him and asked him to judge them. The man was astonished to see the two Imams doing Wudu correctly while his own was incorrect, and in this wise way his Wudu was corrected without embarrassing him (Bihar-ul-Anwar).

mcqs.q: For how long did Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) stay in Makkah after refusing to pledge Bay'at to Yazid?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four months. After Yazid sat on the throne, Imam Husain (RA) was called by the governor of Madinah to pledge Bay'at, but he refused and set out for Makkah, where he stayed for four months while letters from the people of Kufa kept reaching him.

mcqs.q: Whom did Hazrat Imam Husain (RA) send ahead to Kufa to assess the conditions there?
options: His cousin, Hazrat Muslim bin Aqeel (RA)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his cousin Muslim bin Aqeel (RA). Imam Husain (RA) sent him to Kufa to assess the situation; he reported that the people of Kufa had pledged Bay'at, but Ubaidullah bin Ziyad had him martyred before the Imam's arrival.

lessons.title: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family Introduction

  • Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA) is known in Islamic history by his Kuniyyat (teknonym) Abu Ubaidah.
  • His real name is Aamir bin Abdullah bin Al-Jarrah bin Hilal.
  • He belonged to the Banu Fahr branch of the Quraysh, while his mother was from the Banu Harith tribe, who had accepted Islam.
  • The father of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA) was killed in the Battle of Badr in the state of disbelief.

Birth and Attribution to His Grandfather

  • The family of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA) was originally a resident of Makkah, where he was born in the house of Abdullah bin Al-Jarrah Al-Fahri, eleven years after Aam-ul-Feel, and he grew up in Makkah itself.
  • His father was killed in the Battle of Badr in the state of disbelief; therefore, due to Islamic honour, he did not like to include the name of his non-Muslim father with his name, and attributing himself to his grandfather, he began to be called Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah.

Why He Was Called Ameen-e-Hadhihi-ul-Ummah

  • In the ninth year of Hijrah, when some People of the Book from the region of Najran in Yemen came to the Holy Prophet ﷺ for a scholarly debate, and after failing, finally agreed to pay Jizyah, they requested: "O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! You fix Jizyah upon us; we will pay it, and send a trustworthy person with us."
  • Then the Holy Prophet ﷺ, holding the hand of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah, said this about him; therefore, he is called "Ameen-e-Hadhihi-ul-Ummah". (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith 4380)

The title given by the Holy Prophet ﷺ: هَذَا أَمِينُ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ

  • Translation: This person is the Ameen (trustworthy) of this Ummah.

Sariyyah Saif-ul-Bahr — Special Help

  • Note: This event is not stated in the printed lesson text of the book (printed pages 209-213); the following answer is given according to the traditional narration of the famous hadith (Sahih Bukhari).
  • The Holy Prophet ﷺ sent an army of three hundred Companions under the leadership of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah (RA) towards the seashore (Saif-ul-Bahr).
  • On the way, their food ran out, so they began to survive by eating leaves of trees; then, with the special help of Allah Almighty, a huge fish (Al-Anbar) came onto the shore from the sea, eating which they survived for a month.
  • On return, its meat was presented in the service of the Holy Prophet ﷺ; he ate it and said that this is sustenance given by Allah.

Simple Life, Contentment and Zuhd

  • He (RA) used to eat very simple food and wear simple clothes.
  • He also got the position of leading the Islamic army and handling the governorship of Syria, but these things had no effect on his contentment and asceticism (Zuhd).
  • In the time of Hazrat Umar Farooq (RA), when he was the commander of the army on the expedition of Syria and Palestine, one day Ameer-ul-Mu'mineen Hazrat Umar (RA) came to his tent, and saw no valuable goods there except a sword and a shield, and there was no bedding either, so he began to say: "O Abu Ubaidah! Keep some goods of necessity with you."
  • At that time, he (RA) replied with the words given below. (Musannaf Abdur Razzaq, Kitab-ul-Jami', Bab Zuhd-us-Sahabah 11/311)

His reply to Hazrat Umar (RA): يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنَّ هَذَا سَيُبَلِّغُنَا الْمَقِيلَ

  • Translation: O Ameer-ul-Mu'mineen! This very condition of ours will very soon take us to our resting place, that is, Paradise.

Migrations and Passing Away

  • He first migrated towards Abyssinia, and then towards Madinah Munawwarah, attaining the honour of both migrations.
  • In those days, the military camp of the Muslims was in Amwas, in the nearby region of Palestine, when suddenly the disease of plague (Ta'oon) began to spread, in which he passed away in 18 Hijri at the age of 59 years.

mcqs.q: How and when did Hazrat Abu Ubaidah (RA) pass away?
options: He was martyred at Badr at the age of 40
He died of the plague (Ta'oon) at Amwas in 18 Hijri, at the age of 59 years

He was martyred at Uhud at the age of 45
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he died of plague at Amwas in 18 Hijri, aged 59. The Muslim military camp was in Amwas, in the nearby region of Palestine, when the disease of plague (Ta'oon) spread and he passed away in it.

lessons.title: Jabir bin Hayyan (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family, Birth and Names

  • His full name is Jabir bin Hayyan bin Abdullah Al-Kufi (RA); that is, the name of his grandfather was Abdullah.
  • His title is "Sufi" and his Kuniyyat is "Abu Musa"; Europeans know him by the name "Geber".
  • His forefathers belonged to Tus in Khurasan, where he was born in the tribe of Azd in 102 Hijri.
  • Because of these very relations, he used to write, along with his name in his books, "Kufi", "Azdi", "Tusi" or "Sufi".

His Father's Business

  • The father of Jabir, Hayyan bin Abdullah, used to do the business of Attar (perfume).
  • Therefore, on coming to Tus, he opened a "perfume shop" through his ancestral art, where he used to ask about the things present.

Services in the Science of Chemistry — Founder of Chemistry

  • Jabir bin Hayyan (RA) is remembered in the science of chemistry with the title of "Founder of Chemistry".
  • He was the first chemist who divided matter into three parts: plants, animals and minerals; and then divided minerals into three parts: things that turn into vapours, things that melt on fire, and those things which do not melt on heating.
  • Through different ingredients and chemical processes, he prepared a substance which dissolved everything; its name became "acid" (for example: sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid).
  • Through his efforts, the foundation of a new scientific art, "chemistry", was laid.
  • He invented an apparatus named "Qar' Anbiq" for extracting essence (Arq) by heating herbs and fruits, which in today's age is called "Qarnfal" (retort).
  • Many of his Arabic books were translated into Latin, and then into English, and reached Europe; thus, because of him, Europe became acquainted with the science of chemistry.

Famous Inventions

  • His famous inventions are: acids (sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid), the apparatus named "Qar' Anbiq" (which is called "Qarnfal" today), which he invented for extracting essence from herbs and fruits, "carbonate arsenic sulphide", "the method of making dye (Khizab)", "calcining metals", and "methods of polishing iron".
  • Apart from this, he also invented new things in pharmacy and metallurgy, which were not known to anyone before.

Writings

  • Jabir bin Hayyan (RA) is counted among the prolific writers.
  • The number of his treatises and books is more than 232.
  • According to one saying, his writings are more than five hundred, most of which were lost, having fallen victim to the conditions of the age.
  • Many of his Arabic books were translated into Latin, and then from Latin into English, and reached Europe; thus, because of him, Europe became acquainted with the science of chemistry.
  • Whereas his other books are about astronomy, physics, geometry, philosophy and logic, and political science.
  • The names of his books related to the science of chemistry are: "Izah", "Al-Khawas Al-Kabeer" and "Al-Mizan". (A'zam Ulama, Kimiya Jabir bin Hayyan, p. 20)

lessons.title: Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Rozi Dhani (RA)
lessons.notes_html:
Family Lineage

  • His full name is Syed Muhammad Rashid bin Muhammad bin Baqa bin Muhammad Imam Shah.
  • While his title is "Rozi Dhani" and his Kuniyyat is "Abu Yaseen".
  • Hazrat Muhammad Rashid (RA) is the forefather of the Rashidi family of the famous Syed tribe of Sindh.
  • His chain of lineage, after the fourth generation, meets Hazrat Imam Husain, son of Ameer-ul-Mu'mineen Hazrat Ali (may Allah honour his face).
  • The forefather (respected grandfather) of his family is Hazrat Syed Ali Makki (RA), who left his homeland for the propagation of the religion of Islam, and came and adopted residence near the ancient city of Sindh, Sewistan (Sehwan), in Lak Ari; for this reason, his family became famous as Lakiyari.

Birth and the Title Rozi Dhani

  • The birth of Hazrat Pir Muhammad Rashid (RA) took place in Ramadan-ul-Mubarak 1171 Hijri, in a village Raheem Dino Kalhoro, near Khairpur Mirs.
  • It is said that in Ramadan-ul-Mubarak, his habit of drinking milk was such that at the time of Sehri, drinking his mother's milk, he used to spend the whole day like fasting people, and at the Maghrib Azan, he used to cling to his mother again for milk.
  • Because of this habit, he used to be called "Rozi Dhani" (one who keeps fasts); later, attributing him to his shrine (Roza), he was called "Rozi Dhani".

Early Education

  • His father, Hazrat Syed Muhammad Baqa (RA), had fixed a special time for the training of his children, and he had started the series of giving early education at home itself to his sons, including Syed Muhammad Rashid (RA).
  • After that, he kept getting education from Hafiz Zainuddin Mahesar (RA) and Mian Muhammad Akram Ghamro (RA).
  • Then, for further education, he was seated in the Maktab of the famous elder of Shikarpur, Shah Faqirullah Alvi (RA).
  • After that, his father admitted him in the Madrasah of the famous scholar of Kotri Muhammad Kabir, in the present district of Naushahro Feroze, Makhdum Yar Muhammad Siddiqui (RA).
  • And after getting education from there, he was sent to the Ustad-ul-Kul of Arija village, near Larkana, Hazrat Maulana Muhammad Arijvi (RA), from whom he obtained the certificate of completion (Faraghat).

Scholarly Services and Writings

  • Hazrat Muhammad Rashid (RA) was not only perfect in spiritual knowledge, but he had complete command over outward sciences, especially Tafsir, Hadith, Fiqh, Tasawwuf, history, lexicography, and sciences and arts.
  • He had an extraordinary attachment to the Persian and Arabic languages.
  • The state of his vast study and book-reading was such that some book or the other used to be in his hand all the time, and he also had a large scholarly library.
  • To create a love for books among people, he used to say: "Whoever buys expensive books, knowledge will never leave his children."
  • His famous writings are: Jami-ul-Jawami', Persian dictionary (in four large volumes), "Aadab-ul-Mureedeen", "Maktoobat", "Sharh Asma Allah-ul-Husna" and "Jami' Sindhi Kalam".

Spiritual Services

  • He used to keep inviting the common people towards guidance and the religion.
  • He obtained the initial training of Sulook from his respected father, Hazrat Muhammad Baqa Shah (RA), in the Naqshbandi order, and then in the Qadri way, and at the age of twenty-seven, he was appointed the successor of his respected father.
  • Along with his scholarly benefit, his spiritual benefit also proved beneficial for the hearts of thousands of people.
  • After obtaining Khilafat in Sulook from his respected father, he travelled, besides Sindh, to Punjab, and the regions of India: Kutch, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Kathiawar and Balochistan, and kept giving scholarly and spiritual benefit to people.
  • Apart from this, he also played a mujahid-like role to end the wrong customs and innovations spread in society.
  • The collection of his sermons and advice, sayings and conditions, "Malfoozat Sharif", is famous by the name of Pir Muhammad Rashid Rozi Dhani (RA), which his Khalifas compiled.
